name: Amsterdam Merit Scholarships (AMS), University of Amsterdam
organization: University of Amsterdam (UvA), awarded by each faculty / graduate school

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: No separate living stipend in most faculties: the award is roughly the size of the non-EU tuition fee and is paid to you in monthly instalments (Faculty of Science: one AMS of €26,125 for the September 2027 start)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Amounts differ per faculty: Science €26,125 (Sept 2027); Economics and Business = tuition fee + €5,000 allowance (1-year programmes); Social Sciences = equal to the tuition fee; Communication Science = full first-year tuition (one award for 2027-28); Humanities (LLAMS) four €23,500 tuition scholarships and one €40,000 full-ride award for 2027-28; Medicine €4,000; Law amount for 2027-28 to be announced. It is not a tuition-fee waiver: you pay the tuition yourself from the instalments. You must show sufficient funds for all other costs. Two-year programmes: second year depends on results (Science: at least 40 ECTS in year 1).

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Outstanding students who hold a non-EU/EEA passport, are not eligible for Dutch student finance or the reduced EEA tuition rate, and have applied for a UvA Master's programme (Science also excludes Swiss nationals; Communication Science excludes dual nationals with an EU/EEA passport)
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Top 10% of your class. Faculty of Science: generally GPA 3.5/4.0 (US), UK first class / upper division, or Dutch 8+/10; Economics and Business: (magna) cum laude, UK first class or US 3.7; Law: comparable to US 4.0, UK first class or Dutch 8.0; Communication Science: overall GPA of at least 8/10
eligibility.language_requirements: The English requirement of your UvA Master's programme (e.g. Economics and Business: IELTS 7.0 with 7.0 per component, or TOEFL iBT 100)
eligibility.age_limit: No age limit; Faculty of Science requires that you completed your previous academic programme no longer than 3 years ago
eligibility.field_restrictions: UvA Master's programmes in faculties that offer the AMS (Science, Economics and Business, Law, Humanities, Social Sciences, Psychology, Communication Science, Child Development and Education, Medicine); each faculty awards only a few (often one)

nationality.note: Central UvA page: 'Students who hold a non-EU/EEA passport and have applied for a degree programme at the University of Amsterdam may submit an application for an Amsterdam Merit Scholarship.' Applicants must also not be eligible for Dutch student finance (DUO) or the reduced EEA tuition rate, and must not hold another full-coverage scholarship for the same period. Swiss nationals are excluded explicitly by the Faculty of Science and pay the EEA rate, hence the EU/EEA/Switzerland exclusion. Communication Science and Economics and Business exclude anyone who also holds an EU/EEA nationality.

language.note: No AMS-specific test; meet your programme's English requirement (Economics and Business asks IELTS 7.0 with 7.0 per component, TOEFL iBT 100 with 22 per component). Some nationalities/diplomas are exempt per programme.

field.note: Selection is on academic excellence and promise in the field, the quality of your previous institution, a motivation letter and a CV with extracurricular activities (Faculty of Science). Law awards its single AMS by lottery among eligible applicants. The 3-year degree-recency rule is published by the Faculty of Science; other faculties do not state it, so it is a warning here, not a hard fail.

timeline.opening_month: October (Economics and Business: scholarship applications open at the beginning of October; apply through your Master's application)
timeline.typical_deadline: 15 January for most faculties (Science, Economics and Business, Law, Humanities, Communication Science, Child Development and Education); Social Sciences 15 February 2027; Psychology 1 March (2026 date); Medicine (Medical Informatics) 1 June
timeline.interview_period: Selection mostly in March
timeline.result_announcement: Law end of March; Science April; Economics and Business end of April; Social Sciences and Humanities by mid-May

Graduate School of Social Sciences AMS deadline
Graduate School of Psychology AMS deadline (2026 date)
Faculty of Medicine AMS (Medical Informatics, September start)

deadline.note: Deadlines differ per faculty (central AMS page). For the September 2027 start: Faculty of Science 15 January (one AMS of €26,125); Humanities (LLAMS) Master's application by 15 Jan 2027, 23:59 CET, then a form in mid-February; Law 15 January 23:59 CET; Economics and Business 15 January; Communication Science apply by 15 January, questionnaire by 7 February; Child Development and Education before 15 January; Graduate School of Social Sciences 15 Feb 2027, 23:59 CET (only fully, unconditionally admitted students); Psychology page still shows 1 March 2026 (2027 date not yet published); Medicine (Medical Informatics) 1 June for September. Check your programme's faculty page; the AMS request is usually part of the Master's application, so submit the programme application before the deadline.

Complete application to a UvA Master's programme via Studielink and the UvA application form, ticking the scholarship option before the faculty deadline

strategic_tips: Submit your Master's application well before 15 January (or your faculty's date) and tick the scholarship option, because the AMS is decided within the admissions file and incomplete files are dropped. Each faculty offers very few awards (Science: one; Social Sciences gave two to 1.5% of applicants in 2025), so only apply if you are clearly in the top 10% and can prove it with a ranking letter. The award covers about the tuition fee, so budget separately for living costs (the UvA requires proof of funds for the visa).

name: Clarendon Fund Scholarships (University of Oxford)

nationality.note: Official full-time applicants page: 'There are no restrictions by nationality or country of ordinary residence.' Not eligible: holders of a deferred graduate offer, and current Oxford students continuing the same degree. You are considered automatically only if you apply to your Oxford course by its December or January deadline. The ox.ac.uk pages block automated access; they were read through Internet Archive copies of the official pages (May and September 2026).

language.note: Set by your Oxford course: standard level IELTS 7.0 (6.5 per component); higher-level courses need 7.5 (7.0 per component). Usually a condition of the offer; test must be within two years of the course start. Oxford was not accepting TOEFL iBT tests taken on or after 21 Jan 2026 pending review.

timeline.opening_month: September (Oxford course applications for 2027-28 entry were open by late September 2026)
timeline.typical_deadline: Your course's December or January deadline, 12:00 midday UK time (for 2027-28 entry e.g. 2 Dec 2026, 5-7 Jan 2027 or 26-27 Jan 2027 depending on the course)
timeline.interview_period: Departmental interviews (if any) mostly January-March; divisions rank Clarendon nominees in February/March
timeline.result_announcement: Most Clarendon offers are emailed by the end of April; if you have not heard by mid-June, assume you were not selected

extra.label: Early-January course deadlines (e.g. 5-7 Jan)
Late-January course deadlines (e.g. 26-27 Jan)

CV/résumé (usually 1-2 pages)
Statement of purpose / personal statement as specified by the course (word limit set by the course page)
Research proposal or statement of research interests (e.g. max 1,000 words for DPhil Computer Science; limits set by each course)
Three references (usually academic; some courses accept one professional)

name: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships (UK)
organization: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (CSC), funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: £1,712/month, or £2,000/month at universities in the London metropolitan area (rates quoted at current levels)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Full tuition fees (agreed between the CSC and the university); approved return airfare home-UK (not for dependants); study travel grant; £225/year thesis grant; contribution to the visa TB test; Student visa fee and Immigration Health Surcharge paid by the FCDO when applying from outside the UK; child allowance (£622/month first child, £154/month second and third child under 16) only for widowed, divorced or single-parent scholars; disability needs assessment. No separate accommodation payment: the stipend is meant to cover rent and living costs.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Citizens of, or refugees in, 43 eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries (or British Protected Persons) who are permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country; applications from Small Island Developing States are particularly welcome
eligibility.gpa_requirement: By September 2027, a first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) honours standard, or a lower second-class degree plus a relevant postgraduate qualification (usually a Master's). eligibility.field_restrictions: Any one-year full-time taught Master's at a UK university with a CSC part-funding agreement, under one of the six CSC development themes. MBAs are not funded; no support for the overseas fossil-fuel energy sector.

name: DAAD Research Grants - Doctoral Programmes in Germany
organization: German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD), funded by the German Federal Foreign Office

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: €1,400/month
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance; travel allowance (on application only); annual research allowance of €460; possible monthly rent subsidy and family allowance (on application after the start); online German course fees, an optional 2/4/6-month German course before the start, a German course allowance and reimbursement of a TestDaF/DSH fee; disability/chronic-illness subsidy on application. Tuition is not listed as a benefit (doctoral study at German public universities is generally fee-free).

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Citizens of the 129 countries selectable for this programme in the DAAD scholarship database (developing and emerging countries in Africa, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East, the Western Balkans, Eastern Europe and Central Asia, plus e.g. Israel, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Chile, Uruguay)
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Above-average qualifications; selection weighs grade point average, grade development and academic progress
eligibility.language_requirements: For a doctorate in English: TOEFL (paper-based) 550, TOEFL iBT 79, IELTS 6.5, onSET B2 or PTE Academic 59 (not older than 3 years). German skills as needed for the working language; DAAD can fund German courses.
eligibility.age_limit: No age limit, but as a rule your most recent university degree must be no more than six years old at the application deadline (and a doctorate already started no more than three years earlier)
eligibility.field_restrictions: All subjects; individual doctorate with a supervisor or a structured doctoral programme at a state or state-recognised university or non-university research institute in Germany. Human medicine, dentistry and veterinary medicine follow special rules.

nationality.note: The 129 countries of origin offered for this programme ('Doctoral Programmes in Germany, 2027/28') in the official DAAD scholarship database (its country selector and data files, checked 2026-10-25). Not offered for EU/EEA countries, the UK, USA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Switzerland, Gulf states (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain), Singapore, Brunei, Eritrea, Timor-Leste and most small Pacific/Caribbean states. You cannot apply if you have lived in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline. The country page in the database shows your deadline and DAAD office.

language.note: English proof only if the doctorate is in English (IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 79 / PTE 59 / onSET B2, max. 3 years old; TOEFL home edition and IELTS Indicator accepted). German-language projects need German skills; the DAAD may fund a German course before the start.

timeline.typical_deadline: Country-specific, between early August and mid-November of the year before funding starts (2027/28 call: 6 Aug - 16 Nov 2026)
timeline.course_start: October 2027 (a German course before the start can begin from about June)

deadline.label: DAAD portal application (deadline depends on your country; 24:00 CET/CEST)
deadline.note: 2027/28 deadlines by country in the official DAAD database: 6 Aug 2026 Argentina, Chile; 31 Aug 2026 Egypt, Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine, Syria, Iraq, Iran, Israel, Yemen, Afghanistan, Pakistan; 3 Sep 2026 the rest of Latin America and the Caribbean; 24 Sep 2026 most of West, Central and Southern Africa (e.g. Nigeria, Ghana, Cameroon, South Africa, Sudan, Senegal); 30 Sep 2026 Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, Ethiopia, South Sudan; 28 October (no year shown; presumably 28 Oct 2026) South, South-East and East Asia (India, Bangladesh, China, Indonesia, Vietnam, Japan, Korea...); 16 Nov 2026 Turkey, Western Balkans, Ukraine, Belarus, Moldova, the South Caucasus and Central Asia. 31 Aug is used here as the planning date. As of 25 Oct 2026 only the Asian (28 Oct) and Eastern Europe/Central Asia/Turkey (16 Nov) deadlines are still open. DAAD updates deadlines each second quarter and they usually repeat the previous year's pattern.

documents.label: Valid ID with photo, full name, date of birth and country of origin (passport needed for the visa)
Online application form in the DAAD portal
Full curriculum vitae in tabular form (max. 3 pages), plus a list of publications (max. 10 pages) if applicable
