All university degree certificates obtained (Bachelor's, Master's) with final grades; German or English translation if in another language
documents.notes: If your latest degree is not finished yet, upload a provisional document and submit the certificate before the scholarship starts.

documents.label: Transcripts of records (undergraduate and postgraduate) showing individual grades
One recent letter of recommendation from a university teacher on the DAAD form generated in the portal
Proof of English (if the doctorate is in English): TOEFL iBT 79 / IELTS 6.5 / onSET B2 / PTE 59, not older than 3 years
Letter of admission to a structured doctoral programme (can be submitted later)
Optional: employment certificates, internship or volunteering proofs

application_portal_system: DAAD Portal (online; application window 1 June to your country's deadline)
strategic_tips: Find a German supervisor first and develop the proposal and timetable with them: the supervision letter, schedule and ethics declaration all depend on that contact. Check your own country's deadline in the DAAD database (it ranges from August to November) and submit early, because the portal closes at midnight German time. Selection weighs grades and grade trend, proposal quality and feasibility, and your motivation and civic engagement, so give evidence for each.

name: Deutschlandstipendium (Germany Scholarship)
organization: Participating German universities, co-funded by the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) and private sponsors

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: €300/month (€150 from a private sponsor + €150 from the federal government), paid by the university
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Awarded regardless of personal or parental income and nationality; usually for at least two semesters and at most the standard period of study (reviewed yearly). Not counted against BAföG; generally tax- and social-insurance-free. Many universities add mentoring, networking events and internships. Cannot be combined with another merit-based scholarship worth €30/month or more (e.g. a full DAAD scholarship).

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Students of all nationalities enrolled at (or about to start at) a participating state or state-recognised university in Germany
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Talent and high academic achievement (school or university grades), set by each university; social commitment, awards, work experience and overcoming personal or family obstacles also count
eligibility.language_requirements: None for the scholarship itself; your degree programme's language requirements apply
eligibility.field_restrictions: All subjects and degree types, including Master's, second degrees, part-time and dual study; doctoral candidates are excluded

nationality.note: Official FAQ: 'Studierende aller Nationalitäten und aller Fachrichtungen' at a state or state-recognised university that offers the scholarship may apply; prospective students waiting for admission can apply too. Excluded: doctoral candidates, students at federal universities and at public-administration colleges receiving civil-service pay. Each university decides whether to take part and sets its own criteria and deadlines.

language.note: No language test for the scholarship; meet your programme's German or English requirement.

timeline.opening_month: Varies by university (often April-August, for the following winter semester)
timeline.typical_deadline: Set by each university, mostly between May and September for the winter semester (e.g. Univ. Bonn 18 May 2026; TU Braunschweig 1-30 June 2026)

deadline.label: Your university's Deutschlandstipendium call (each university sets its own window)
deadline.note: There is no national deadline: the federal site says to ask your university about its procedure and deadlines. Examples for the 2026/27 funding year on official university pages: University of Bonn until 18 May 2026; TU Braunschweig 1-30 June 2026 (Heidelberg's portal had already closed when checked). Other universities run calls as late as September. 30 June is used here only as a planning date; look up your university's call (often published in spring) and check whether first-semester/Master's starters can apply before enrolling.

documents.label: Online application on your university's Deutschlandstipendium portal (often with a motivation section and declaration)
Letter of motivation (format and length set by the university)
Tabular curriculum vitae
Proof of performance: transcript of records (current students) or, for new Master's students, the bachelor's transcript/overview of grades
Bachelor's certificate (if starting a Master's)
School-leaving certificate / higher education entrance qualification (if starting a Bachelor's)
Evidence of social commitment, awards, internships or other achievements, if available
Letter of recommendation (only some universities ask for one)

application_portal_system: Each participating university's own application portal or procedure
strategic_tips: Look up your target university's call as soon as you apply for admission: many calls run in spring or early summer, and new students can often apply before enrolling. Selection rewards grades plus social engagement and obstacles you have overcome, so document volunteering, awards and your personal story. It is only €300/month and cannot be stacked with another merit scholarship worth €30+/month, so treat it as a supplement for self-funded study.

name: Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarships for International Graduate and PhD Students (Germany)
organization: Heinrich-Böll-Stiftung (Studienwerk), funded by the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) and the Federal Foreign Office

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: International Master's students: €992/month base scholarship; non-EU PhD candidates: €1,400/month plus €100/month mobility allowance (EU nationals follow different, BAföG-style rates)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Master's (Foreign Office-funded): health insurance allowance up to €100/month; optional components depending on your situation: reimbursement of tuition fees in Germany up to €10,000/year, German language course fees, €38/month fringe benefits, family and child allowances. PhD (non-EU): individual allowances; tuition fees are not funded. Seminars, mentoring and an alumni network. Additional income is offset against the scholarship.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: International students and PhD candidates from the EU and DAC-list countries; priority for applicants from DAC countries who have not yet taken up residence in Germany when they apply
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Very good school and university academic record (no numeric minimum published)
eligibility.language_requirements: Good or very good German: at least level B2 or DSH 1, with a certificate (required at application)
eligibility.field_restrictions: All disciplines at state or state-recognised universities in Germany. Master's: full-time programmes with a standard duration of at least four semesters, and you must apply before the Master's starts. PhD: subjects related to the foundation's focal points get priority.

nationality.note: Official English page: 'graduate and PhD scholarships to international students and PhD candidates from the EU and DAC countries'; priority for DAC-country applicants still living abroad. The German page says non-EU PhD candidates in general may apply, with DAC applicants given priority. These rules are for applicants who earned their university entrance qualification and first degree abroad; Germans and people educated in Germany follow the domestic programme. Refugees can apply regardless of asylum status. Applicants rejected after the final interview stage may not reapply.

language.note: German B2 or DSH 1 certificate is compulsory with the application, even for English-taught programmes. Application documents must be in German (expert and personal references may be in English).

field.note: Open to all subjects. The foundation looks for people who share its ideals (democracy, ecology, solidarity, non-violence) and show social and political commitment. For PhDs, topics linked to the foundation's focal areas get priority.

timeline.opening_month: 15 January (spring round) and 15 July (autumn round); the portal opens about 6 weeks before each deadline
timeline.typical_deadline: 1 March and 1 September (binding, no exceptions)
timeline.interview_period: Interview with a liaison lecturer by about mid-May (March round) or mid-November (September round); online committee interview May-July or December-February
timeline.course_start: Funding starts at the latest on 1 October (March round) or 1 April (September round)

deadline.label: Spring round online application (portal open 15 Jan - 1 Mar)

extra.label: Autumn round (funding from April of the next year)

deadline.note: Official next deadlines: Spring 2027 round 15 Jan - 1 Mar 2027 (funding by 1 Oct 2027, fits a winter-semester 2027 start); Fall 2027 round 15 Jul - 1 Sep 2027. The Fall 2026 round (deadline 1 Sep 2026) has passed. All documents, including references sent directly by referees, must arrive by the deadline. Master's applicants must apply before their Master's begins.

documents.label: Passport (needed for the application and the visa)
documents.notes: Not always on the official list, but required to apply and for the visa.

documents.label: Application form in German (Bewerbungsbogen A1-2 for Master's / A2-2 for PhD), filled in with Adobe Acrobat Reader and uploaded to the online portal
documents.notes: Contains your personal data and CV. Space is limited: answers must fit the boxes and stay legible when printed.

documents.label: Motivation sections of the application form: why the Heinrich Böll Foundation, why your subject (or your PhD project outline), and your social commitment and political interests
Certificate of German proficiency: at least B2 or DSH 1 (absolutely necessary)
Copy of your university entrance qualification (Abitur/baccalaureate) with German or English certified translation if needed
Certified copy of your degree certificate with German or English translation and an explanation of the grading if it differs from the German system
Transcript of records (if no average grade is given, calculate and state it yourself)
Expert report (academic reference) from a university lecturer on the foundation's form A1-3b / A2-3b, ideally from your target German university or the same programme elsewhere
documents.notes: Must come from a different person than the social-commitment reference; can be emailed by the referee directly to studienwerk@boell.de by the deadline.

documents.label: Reference on your social commitment (form A1-4b) from someone who knows your engagement well, preferably representing an institution or organisation (not a friend or family member)

Detailed exposé of your PhD project (max. 10 pages: up to 8 pages project and bibliography, 1 page thesis structure, 1 page research plan and timetable of at most 36 months with preliminary work done)
Certification by the university of admission to doctoral studies (or a justified confirmation by the supervisor)
Enrolment certificate or confirmation of admission to the Master's programme (may be sent later, at the latest by the final-stage interview)

application_portal_system: Heinrich Böll Foundation online application portal (opens about 6 weeks before each deadline)
strategic_tips: This is a political foundation: show documented social or political engagement and explain clearly how your values connect to the foundation's ideals of democracy, ecology, solidarity and non-violence. Get your German to B2/DSH 1 before applying, because the certificate is compulsory even for English-taught programmes. Ask a professor at your target German university for the expert report, and have a different person (an organisation you volunteered with) write the social-commitment reference.
program_status_note: The foundation announced: 'Note for Master's students: Starting March 1, 2027, we will only accept applications for first-cycle programs' (German page: from 1 March 2027 only applications for the first degree, Erststudium). Its page for applicants educated abroad still lists the Master's route for the Spring 2027 round, so it is unclear whether international Master's applicants can still apply from March 2027. PhD scholarships are not affected. Confirm with studienwerk@boell.de before preparing a Master's application.

name: Knight-Hennessy Scholars (Stanford University)
organization: Knight-Hennessy Scholars, Stanford University

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Stipend for living and academic expenses (room and board, books, supplies, local transport, personal expenses); amount not published on the KHS funding page
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Fellowship covering tuition and associated fees for up to three years; travel stipend for one economy round trip to Stanford per year; one-time relocation stipend for new scholars; supplemental funds for academic enrichment (e.g. conferences) in years 2-3. Degrees longer than three years (PhD, MD) are funded beyond year 3 by the department's standard funding commitment. Stipends are taxable. Health insurance and visa costs are not listed separately on the funding page.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Citizens and residents of all countries (undocumented and DACA students also eligible); no quotas by discipline, programme or world region
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No minimum GPA or test score for KHS; you must meet your Stanford graduate programme's requirements and hold a U.S. bachelor's degree or equivalent
eligibility.language_requirements: No KHS minimum; your Stanford programme's requirement applies (for most programmes TOEFL 90 if taken before 21 Jan 2026 / 5.5 if taken on or after, or IELTS 7)
eligibility.age_limit: No age limit, but your first bachelor's degree must be earned in January 2020 or later to enrol in 2027 (two extra years for military service)
eligibility.field_restrictions: Any full-time Stanford graduate degree (MA, MS, MBA, MD, JD, MFA, MPP, PhD, DMA...); not the Honors Cooperative Program, Master of Liberal Arts, JSD, MLS, coterminal degrees, or a current PhD student adding an MA/MS in their discipline

nationality.note: Official eligibility page (2027 cohort): 'We encourage citizens and residents of all countries to apply.' You must apply separately and concurrently to KHS and to a full-time Stanford graduate programme (or hold a deferred offer to start in the same year, or be a first-year Stanford PhD student joining KHS in year 2).

language.note: KHS sets no minimum; you report the scores your Stanford programme requires. Most programmes: TOEFL 90 (before 21 Jan 2026) / 5.5 (on or after), IELTS 7. Check your programme's waiver rules.

timeline.opening_month: June (application for the 2027 cohort opened 1 June 2026; the 2028 cohort opens in summer 2027)
timeline.typical_deadline: Early October (6 Oct 2026, 1:00 pm Pacific Time, for the 2027 cohort); Stanford programme application by the earlier of its KHS deadline or 1 December
timeline.interview_period: Video statement invitations on a rolling basis in January; finalists notified 27 Jan 2027

deadline.label: Knight-Hennessy Scholars application (1:00 pm Pacific Time)

extra.label: Stanford graduate programme application (by 1 Dec or the programme's earlier KHS deadline)

deadline.note: 2027 cohort: KHS application opened 1 Jun 2026 and closed 6 Oct 2026, 1:00 pm PT (same for all programmes); the official page now says it is closed. The separate Stanford programme application is due by the earlier of the programme's deadline for KHS applicants or 1 Dec 2026 (MBA applicants must use Round 1). The 2028 cohort application opens in summer 2027; its deadline is not yet published (expect early October 2027).

documents.label: Passport (needed for the application and the visa)
documents.notes: Not always on the official list, but required to apply and for the visa.

documents.label: KHS online application form (no application fee)
documents.notes: Shortlisted applicants are later invited to submit a video statement (January).

documents.label: Separate application to a full-time Stanford graduate degree programme (by the earlier of its KHS deadline or 1 December)
documents.notes: Most Stanford programmes charge an application fee; KHS cannot waive it.

documents.label: One-page resume (US Letter, reverse-chronological, no photos or hyperlinks)
Transcripts for each institution attended one academic year or longer (unofficial copies or self-reported form accepted; official English translation if not in English)
Diploma showing degree conferred and date, only if your transcript does not show it
Two recommendation letters (academic, community or professional) addressing the three KHS criteria
documents.notes: Due by the application deadline; you may not draft, edit or translate them.

documents.label: Three short answers and one essay
items: Describe your short-term and long-term academic and professional intentions (250 words)
Tell us when you a) engaged with someone with a different perspective, b) acted with courage, and c) fell short of expectations (250 words combined)
Eight improbable facts about you (150 words combined)
Essay: Connect the dots. How have the influences in your life shaped you? (550 words)

documents.label: GRE/GMAT or other test scores, only if your Stanford programme requires them
TOEFL/IELTS scores if your Stanford programme requires them (most do for non-native speakers), reported to KHS by the later of the two deadlines
documents.notes: Most programmes accept TOEFL; most (not all) accept IELTS. You can add scores after submitting via your status page.

application_portal_system: Knight-Hennessy Scholars online application + separate Stanford Graduate Admissions application
strategic_tips: KHS selects on three criteria: independence of thought, purposeful leadership and civic mindset, so every short answer, the essay and both letters should show concrete evidence of them rather than a list of achievements. Plan the two applications together: the KHS deadline (early October) comes two months before the Stanford programme deadline, and your recommenders should tailor separate letters for each. Check the bachelor's-date rule first (degree from January 2020 or later for 2027; one year later for each later cohort).

name: Romanian Government Scholarships for Foreign Citizens (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
organization: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Romania with the Ministry of Education and Research (Government Decision no. 288/1993)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Monthly scholarship 'in accordance with the legislation in force' (amount not stated on the official portal; paid in Romanian lei)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Tuition for the Romanian-language preparatory year and for the degree (one study cycle); monthly scholarship during the preparatory year and the degree; accommodation in student dormitories within the subsidy allocated by the Ministry of Education (subject to available places); exemption from application, language-test, doctoral admission and aptitude-test fees. Scholars pay their own visa costs and international travel.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Foreign citizens from all non-EU countries, except people of Romanian origin or from Romanian historical communities (separate programme), people who requested or hold protection in Romania, stateless persons officially resident in Romania, diplomatic/consular staff and their families, staff of international organisations in Romania and their families, and holders of a Romanian state scholarship for the same study cycle
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Average of at least 7 (seven) on the Romanian scale, or 'Good', for the last school graduated
eligibility.language_requirements: Bachelor's and Master's are taught only in Romanian, with a funded Romanian-language preparatory year for those who do not speak it; PhD can be in Romanian or a foreign language set by the doctoral school
eligibility.field_restrictions: All fields except Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy

nationality.note: Official portal: 'Foreign citizens from all non-EU countries', with the exceptions listed in eligible_nationalities (Romanian-origin applicants, people with protection in Romania, stateless residents, diplomatic staff and families, international-organisation staff in Romania, current Romanian state scholars in the same cycle). No age limit. Only one application per call.

language.note: No language test to apply. Bachelor's/Master's are taught in Romanian after a funded preparatory year (exempt with Romanian B1, a passed Romanian test, or 3+ years of schooling in Romanian). PhD may be taught in English or another language chosen by the doctoral school.

field.note: Scholarships are NOT awarded in Medicine, Dental Medicine or Pharmacy.

timeline.interview_period: PhD applicants must pass the doctoral school's admission interview (and have a tutor's written agreement before applying); no interview is stated for Bachelor/Master
timeline.course_start: October (academic year usually begins 1 October; preparatory year first if needed)

deadline.label: Online application on the Study in Romania scholarship platform
deadline.note: 2026/27 call: applications 16 Feb - 31 Mar 2026, results around 15 Jul 2026 (official portal). The 2027/28 call is not yet published; if the pattern repeats, expect mid-February to 31 March 2027. Applications sent by email, post, to ministries or embassies are rejected; use only the online platform. The MFA website (mae.ro) could not be loaded when checked, so dates come from the official Study in Romania scholarship portal.

documents.label: Online application on scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro (one application per call), including a signed GDPR consent
Copy of the first three pages of a valid passport
Copy of birth certificate (or equivalent) with authorised translation into English, French, Spanish or Romanian if needed
Baccalaureate diploma or equivalent, apostilled/authenticated, with authorised translation if needed
Bachelor's (and Master's, for PhD) diplomas, apostilled/authenticated, with authorised translation if needed (or a certificate of passing the final exam if the diploma is not yet issued)
Transcripts of completed studies, apostilled/authenticated, with authorised translation if needed
Curriculum Vitae in English, French or Romanian
Letter of intent with list of scientific works and publications and a detailed description of the proposed research project (English, French or Romanian)
Written agreement of a doctoral tutor who is a member of the chosen doctoral school
Romanian B1 certificate or preparatory-year completion certificate (only if you want to skip the preparatory year)
Medical certificate (fit for study, free of contagious diseases) with authorised translation, presented at enrolment
Letter of acceptance for studies in Romania (issued by the Ministry of Education after selection; needed for the long-stay visa)

application_portal_system: Study in Romania scholarship platform (scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro), in English or French
strategic_tips: Have your diplomas and transcripts apostilled (or authenticated by your education ministry) and translated well before February, because the call is short (mid-February to 31 March). For Bachelor's and Master's you will study in Romanian after a funded preparatory year, so plan for an extra year; PhD applicants can choose English but must secure a doctoral tutor's written agreement before applying. Medicine, dentistry and pharmacy are excluded.

name: ADB-Japan Scholarship Program (ADB-JSP)
country: Asia-Pacific (Designated Institutions in Japan, Hong Kong, India, Pakistan, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Hawaii, USA)
organization: Asian Development Bank (ADB), financed by the Government of Japan

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Monthly subsistence and housing allowance (amount not published by ADB; varies by institution)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Full tuition, monthly subsistence and housing allowance, allowance for books and instructional materials, medical insurance and travel expenses. A thesis grant may be available for research students; preparatory language or computer courses may be covered in special cases. One year, extendable to a second year on satisfactory performance (maximum two years for a master's). Not covered: family/dependants, extra-curricular courses, extra travel, field trips, workshops, internships, computers. Visa costs are not mentioned.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Citizens of the 40 ADB borrowing members that are also Japanese ODA scholarship-eligible (South, Southeast and Central Asia, the Caucasus, Mongolia and the Pacific), with no dual citizenship of a developed country, who live and work in their home country.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Bachelor's degree or equivalent with a superior academic record (no numeric minimum published).
eligibility.language_requirements: Proficiency in oral and written English; the Designated Institution sets the test and minimum score.
eligibility.age_limit: Not more than 35 years old at the time of application (waived only in exceptional cases with the Government of Japan's endorsement).
eligibility.field_restrictions: Only the 'Approved Fields of Study' at each Designated Institution: economics, business and management, science and technology, engineering, agriculture, environment, health, education, law and public policy, development studies and other development-related fields.
eligibility.return_obligation: Must return and work in your home country for at least 2 years after the program (signed Acceptance of Scholarship Award); 2-year employment restriction at the ADB Group after the program.

nationality.note: Citizenship list from the official ADB-JSP page ('Federated States of Micronesia', 'Kyrgyz Republic', 'Lao PDR', 'Naoero' (Nauru) and 'Viet Nam' normalised). Also required: no dual citizenship of a developed country, not living or working outside your home country, not already enrolled in a graduate program, not ADB staff/consultant or close relative, not staff of a Designated Institution, no earlier ADB-JSP award. In principle ADB does not support applicants who studied abroad before or who seek a second master's degree; women and applicants with less financial capacity get preference.

language.note: Each Designated Institution sets its own English requirement.

field.note: Only courses listed as 'Approved Fields of Study' at each Designated Institution; the field should match your academic background and work, and ADB's Strategy 2030 or Japan's ODA priorities.

timeline.opening_month: Varies by institution (you apply through the institution's admission process)
timeline.typical_deadline: Set by each Designated Institution: mostly November to early January for August-October intakes (some as early as October or as late as March-April); send the application at least 6 months before the program starts
timeline.result_announcement: Institution ranks applicants, ADB recommends, the Japanese Executive Director approves; the institution informs applicants
timeline.course_start: Mostly August-October (some April or January intakes)

deadline.label: Designated Institution admission + ADB-JSP information sheet (varies by institution)
deadline.note: There is no single ADB deadline; 1 December is only a planning placeholder. Examples from the official institution list (normal month, applicable every year): HKU January; IIT Delhi December; Hitotsubashi APP early January; International University of Japan early January; Keio November-January; Kobe early January; Kyoto November (Oct intake); GRIPS November; Tohoku early January; UNU-IAS early February; Science Tokyo early April; LUMS 27 February (round 1); NUS 15 December-31 January; AIM August (January intake). Check the exact date and intake with your institution.

documents.label: Admission application to an approved master's course at an ADB-JSP Designated Institution, stating that you want to be considered for ADB-JSP
ADB-JSP Information Sheet (sent to the institution with your admission application)
documents.notes: Includes your proposed study plan, salary and family income, and 'why this area of study at this institution'.

documents.label: Copies of all academic records
Bachelor's degree certificate (superior academic record)
Latest Certificate of Employment showing your annual/monthly salary (signed/stamped), proving 2+ years of full-time work after your degree
Latest income tax return or salary certification, plus certification of family income (both parents, or spouse if married; local agency certificate if retired, deceased or unemployed)
English proficiency proof as required by the Designated Institution
documents.notes: The test and minimum score depend on the institution.

documents.label: Acceptance of Scholarship Award (signed; you agree to return home and work there for at least 2 years)

application_portal_system: No separate ADB application: apply through the chosen Designated Institution's admission process with the ADB-JSP Information Sheet
strategic_tips: Choose a Designated Institution outside your own country (applicants to an institution in their own country may not be selected) and an approved course that clearly follows from your degree and 2+ years of work. Apply to the institution about 6-10 months before the intake, attach the Information Sheet, and frame your goals around ADB Strategy 2030 or Japan's ODA priorities (climate, health coverage, infrastructure, public finance, poverty). You may apply to more than one institution, but declare it on the form.

name: Government of Brunei Darussalam Scholarship for Foreign Students (BDGS)
organization: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Brunei Darussalam

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: BND 500/month personal allowance + BND 150/month meals allowance
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Exemption from tuition, acceptance, examination, registration and orientation fees; economy air ticket to Brunei at the start and back home at the end; accommodation at the university/polytechnic residential college; BND 600/year book allowance; baggage allowance on completion (BND 250 within ASEAN, BND 500 outside); comprehensive insurance (extra insurance at your own cost is advised). No allowances for family members. Visa costs are not mentioned.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Foreign students. Bruneians, Brunei permanent residents and international students who are studying or have studied at a Brunei tertiary institution are NOT eligible; the scholarship is primarily for first-time students in Brunei.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No minimum GPA published; admission depends on the chosen institution and program.
eligibility.language_requirements: Credit 6 in GCE 'O' Level English, grade C in IGCSE English (as a second language), IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL 550 (paper-based). Institutions may also test English, Malay or Arabic.
eligibility.age_limit: Not more than 25 for Diploma and Undergraduate programs, and not more than 35 for Master's programs, on 1 July of the year the course starts.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Programs listed as BDGS-eligible at Universiti Brunei Darussalam (UBD), Universiti Islam Sultan Sharif Ali (UNISSA), Universiti Teknologi Brunei (UTB), Kolej Universiti Perguruan Ugama Seri Begawan (KUPU SB) and Politeknik Brunei (PB).
eligibility.return_obligation: You must leave Brunei immediately after completing the program.

nationality.note: The 2026/2027 call sets no country list: it is open to foreign students, but excludes Bruneians, Brunei permanent residents and international students who are studying or have studied at a Brunei tertiary institution.

language.note: Alternatives: GCE O Level English credit 6, IGCSE English (second language) grade C, or TOEFL 550 (paper-based).

field.note: Only programs listed as BDGS-eligible by the five participating institutions.

timeline.typical_deadline: 15 February, 23:59 Brunei time (2026/2027 call)
timeline.interview_period: Shortlisted applicants may be interviewed and given an English/Malay/Arabic test by the institution
timeline.result_announcement: Successful applicants are contacted; unsuccessful ones are notified by email

deadline.label: BDGS online registration (23:59 Brunei time)
deadline.note: 2026/2027 call: opened 15 Dec 2025, closed 15 Feb 2026 at 23:59 Brunei time (MFA page and official flyer shared by the German Embassy Bandar Seri Begawan). The 2027/2028 call is not announced yet (the MFA page still shows 2026/2027); expect a similar mid-December to mid-February window. UBD and UTB applicants must also apply on the university's own portal.

documents.label: BDGS online application form (MFA Brunei)
Separate online application to the university (UBD: apply.ubd.edu.bn; UTB: apply.utb.edu.bn)
documents.notes: Required only if you choose UBD or UTB.

documents.label: Identification card
Certified true copy of passport
Certified true copy of birth certificate (certified English translation if not in English)
Certified true copies of transcripts (certified English translation if not in English)
Certified true copy of your degree certificate
Certified true copy of your school-leaving certificate
IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL 550 (paper-based), or GCE O Level English credit 6 / IGCSE English grade C
References and recommendations from two referees
Signed declaration accepting the scholarship terms and conditions (on acceptance)

application_portal_system: BDGS online application system (Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Brunei) plus UBD/UTB admission portals
strategic_tips: Choose your program from the BDGS-eligible lists of the five institutions before applying, and for UBD or UTB submit the university's own application as well. Get certified true copies (and certified English translations) of your passport, birth certificate and academic records ready in December, since the window is only about two months. Watch the age cut-off: 35 for Master's (25 for Diploma/Bachelor) on 1 July of the start year.

name: Hamad Bin Khalifa University (HBKU) Graduate Scholarships
organization: Hamad Bin Khalifa University (Qatar Foundation, Education City, Doha)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: International PhD: QAR 9,000/month (up to 45 months); International Master's: QAR 7,000/month (up to 21 months), for selected full-time students serving as research/teaching assistants
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Tuition waiver for HBKU-sponsored students: 100% for PhD (STEM and SHAPE) and S.J.D.; 75% for STEM MS programs (CSE, CHLS); 60% for SHAPE MS/MA (CIS, CHSS, CPP) and J.D.; 0% for LL.M., MS Economics and certificates. One round-trip airfare for international students (inbound at start, outbound at graduation). Stipend holders work 10 h/week as RAs and may earn extra as TAs (QAR 50/h). Housing (QF dorms or private) is paid from the stipend; meals are not included. Health insurance and visa costs are not mentioned on the scholarship page. Awards depend on available funds and are reviewed yearly.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: All nationalities. International applicants have an earlier deadline (1 Feb 2027) than Qatari and resident applicants seeking funding (15 Mar 2027). Stipend rates differ for Qatari, international and local (resident) students.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: College of Science and Engineering: minimum 3.0/4.0 from a recognized university (other colleges set their own criteria). Master's applicants need a bachelor's; PhD applicants a master's.
eligibility.language_requirements: IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 79 (College of Science and Engineering); exemptions are possible in some cases via admissions.hbku.edu.qa. GRE/GMAT required for some PhD programs (e.g. Sustainable Energy, Sustainable Environment) and optional elsewhere.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Graduate programs of HBKU's colleges: Islamic Studies, Humanities and Social Sciences, Science and Engineering, Law, Health and Life Sciences, Public Policy, and the School of Economics and Management (MS Economics is self-funded). Each program lists required undergraduate fields.
eligibility.return_obligation: None

nationality.note: Open to all nationalities; Qatari nationals and Qatar residents have separate deadlines and stipend rates (local stipends are limited). Full-time working professionals, and part-time workers above 40% of full-time hours, are not eligible for stipends.

language.note: IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 79 in the College of Science and Engineering; exemption rules on admissions.hbku.edu.qa. Scores are sent directly by the test body (TOEFL code 4981).

field.note: Check the 'required field of study' of your program; e.g. Data Science and Engineering needs computer science, engineering, mathematics or related degrees.

timeline.typical_deadline: 1 February for international applicants (1 Feb 2027); 15 March for Qatari/resident applicants seeking funding
timeline.result_announcement: Colleges notify applicants after review; scholarship details come by email with the offer

deadline.label: HBKU graduate application deadline for international applicants

extra.label: Deadline for Qatari and resident applicants who want funding

deadline.note: Fall 2027 dates on the official Graduate Admissions page: application opened 1 Oct 2026; international applicants 1 Feb 2027; Qatari and resident applicants seeking funding 15 Mar 2027. There is no separate scholarship application: you are considered for tuition waivers and stipends during admission. Up to two applications per academic year.

documents.label: HBKU online graduate application (up to 2 programs per year; QAR 250 non-refundable fee)
Official electronic transcripts with an explanation of the grading system (official translation if not in English or Arabic)
Final transcripts and graduation statements for all previous university studies
IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 79, sent directly to HBKU (TOEFL code 4981)
GRE/GMAT (required for some PhD programs such as Sustainable Energy and Sustainable Environment; optional or recommended elsewhere)
Letter of recommendation 1 of 2: from an academic referee
Letter of recommendation 2 of 2
Personal statement of interest (300-500 words): why this program, how it serves your goals, your research interests and achievements
Resume/CV (qualifications, experience, publications, research projects, awards, conference presentations)
Electronic copy of passport (plus valid Qatari ID for nationals and residents)

application_portal_system: HBKU online admissions portal (Ellucian CRM Recruit, hbkuqa.elluciancrmrecruit.com)
strategic_tips: International applicants must apply by 1 February, six weeks before residents, and scholarships are decided during admission, so the personal statement and research fit drive both. PhD awards are the strongest (100% tuition + QAR 9,000/month); most master's awards waive only 60-75% of tuition, and housing comes out of the stipend, so budget for the remainder. Contact a potential supervisor in your target division before applying, especially for research-heavy programs.

name: ICCR Scholarships for Foreign Nationals (A2A portal)
organization: Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Monthly stipend plus House Rent Allowance (HRA) per ICCR financial norms (amounts shown on the A2A portal, not on the public pages)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Tuition fee/other compulsory fees paid to the university, stipend, HRA, contingent allowance and thesis/dissertation allowance. Return economy airfare to the airport nearest the place of study under most schemes (not under the Cultural Exchange scheme except for Mexico and Turkmenistan). Students pay hostel/private accommodation and mess charges, deposits, certificate and immigration (FRRO) fees, and must buy medical insurance of at least INR 500,000 at their own cost. Carry about USD 1,500 for the first 2-3 months before allowances start.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Nationals of countries with slots under one of ICCR's country schemes (2026-27: about 4,540 slots across 18 schemes, e.g. India-Africa Maitri for 54 African countries, Atal Bihari Vajpayee General Scheme for 116 countries, Mekong Ganga, Suborno Jayanti for Bangladesh, Aid to Sri Lanka). Many countries have only 1-2 slots.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No ICCR minimum; each Indian university applies its own admission criteria.
eligibility.language_requirements: Good English (teaching is in English): a 500-word English essay on a topic listed on the A2A portal is mandatory; TOEFL/IELTS scores are optional; the Indian Mission may set its own English criteria.
eligibility.age_limit: As on 1 July: minimum 18; maximum 35 for UG, PG, certificate and diploma courses; maximum 40 for PhD; no upper limit for Hindi, Sanskrit and Indian performing arts (2026-27 guidelines).
eligibility.field_restrictions: Courses at ICCR-empanelled Indian public (central/state) universities and institutes only (134 for 2026-27). No medicine, para-medical courses (nursing, physiotherapy, etc.), law or integrated courses; no B.Tech at IITs; GMAT needed for MBA at some universities. AYUSH (Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, Homoeopathy) is under separate AYUSH schemes.
eligibility.return_obligation: You must leave India after receiving your final results and before your residential permit expires.

nationality.note: Union of the country lists of the 2026-27 ICCR schemes that fund UG/PG/PhD study in India: India-Africa Maitri (54 African countries), Atal Bihari Vajpayee General (116 countries), Mekong Ganga (Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam), Commonwealth (Canada, Guyana, New Zealand, UK), Cultural Exchange (23 countries; Bulgaria, Cyprus, Israel, Mexico, Spain etc. only for some levels), and single-country schemes for Nepal (PG/PhD only), Maldives, Mongolia, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. Not included: China (only a one-year Hindi certificate), Afghanistan (online e-scholarship only), Philippines (only Quad STEM B.Tech slots), Pakistan (no scheme listed). Guadeloupe and Reunion (French territories) have their own slots. The Lata Mangeshkar Dance & Music scheme (Indian culture, dance, music, yoga; 100 slots) is open to all countries. PIO/OCI holders must have schooled abroad and not studied in India in the previous 3 (PG) / 5 (PhD) years. The 2027-28 allocation is not published yet; re-verify.

language.note: No fixed test score: a mandatory 500-word English essay on the A2A portal; TOEFL/IELTS optional; the Indian Mission may check English.

field.note: Any course at an empanelled public university except medicine, para-medical, law and integrated programs.

timeline.opening_month: Late February (A2A portal opened 27 Feb 2026 for 2026-27)
timeline.typical_deadline: Mid-April (15 Apr 2026, extended to 22 Apr 2026, for 2026-27)
timeline.interview_period: Some universities interview PhD applicants
timeline.result_announcement: Universities confirm provisional admission by mid-May; Indian Missions select and send offers by late May/early June (second round 1-10 June 2026)

deadline.label: A2A portal: last date for students to apply
deadline.note: 2026-27 cycle: the A2A portal opened 27 Feb 2026 with a 15 Apr 2026 student deadline (Embassy of India Abu Dhabi and Baghdad notices), later extended to 22 Apr 2026 (ICCR 'Revised Timelines', published by the Consulate General of India, Sao Paulo). Universities scrutinised until 15 May, Missions selected until 31 May, second round 1-10 June, joining June-August 2026. The 2027-28 timeline is not announced yet; expect a similar late-Feb to mid-April window, and check your Indian Embassy's notice.

documents.label: One online application on the A2A portal with up to 5 university/course choices in order of preference
documents.notes: Multiple applications in the same year lead to rejection. Performing-arts applicants upload a recent video/audio/YouTube link of their performance.

documents.label: 500-word essay in English on one of the topics listed on the A2A portal
Passport valid for at least 2 years as on 1 July of the admission year
Passport-size photograph on a white background with both ears visible
Academic transcripts/mark sheets with English translation (certified copies of translations if not in English)
documents.notes: Without an English transcript the application is rejected.

documents.label: Degree certificate of the last qualifying degree (with English translation)
12th-grade (10+2) school-leaving certificate (Maths, Physics, Chemistry for science/engineering; Biology, Physics, Chemistry for biology-based courses)
Synopsis (proposal) of your PhD research topic
TOEFL/IELTS score (optional; upload if you have one)
GMAT score (MBA applicants, where the university requires it)
Medical Fitness Certificate with test reports and vaccinations, uploaded after accepting the offer
Certified transcript/syllabus of the last qualifying examination (bring to India for verification)
AIU Equivalence Certificate (Association of Indian Universities), if your university requires it

application_portal_system: ICCR A2A (Admissions to Alumni) Scholarship Portal, a2ascholarships.iccr.gov.in; selection by the Indian Embassy/High Commission in your country; visa via the Study in India (SII) portal
strategic_tips: Check how many slots your country has under its scheme on the ICCR schemes page (often only 1-5 outside Africa and South Asia) and contact the Indian Embassy early. Use all 5 choices, matching each course's entry rules on the university website, because the university must upload a provisional admission before the Mission can select you. Budget for medical insurance (INR 500,000 cover) and about USD 1,500 for the first months, which the scholarship does not cover.

name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP)
country: Multi-country (participating master's programs in the United States, United Kingdom, Netherlands, France, Japan, Australia and Cote d'Ivoire)
organization: World Bank (Development Economics Vice Presidency), funded by the Government of Japan

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Monthly subsistence allowance covering all living expenses (accommodation, food, books); amount depends on the host country and is not disclosed to applicants
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Economy-class round trip between your home country and the host university plus a US$600 travel allowance for each trip; tuition and basic medical insurance obtained through the university. Covers the program length or two years, whichever is less. Not covered: visa and residence-permit costs, family members, research/field trips, workshops, internships, computers, language training outside the program.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Nationals of the World Bank member developing countries on the 2027 JJ/WBGSP list (Annex 1), with no dual citizenship of any developed country. Japanese nationals apply through a separate JJ/WBGSP track.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No minimum GPA published (education background is 10% of the score). Bachelor's degree earned at least 3 years before the application deadline.
eligibility.language_requirements: No JJ/WBGSP test. You must hold an unconditional admission to a participating program, so you must already meet that program's English (or other teaching language) requirement; offers conditional on a language score are not accepted.
eligibility.age_limit: None
eligibility.field_restrictions: Only the 44 JJ/WBGSP participating master's programs (2027) in development-related fields: economic and public policy, public administration, public health, tax policy, water, urban change, climate and environment, infrastructure, development studies, agriculture.
eligibility.return_obligation: Scholars commit to return to their home country to apply their skills to its development (the FAQ says plans such as a later PhD do not stop you from applying; explain your plans in the Statement of Purpose).

nationality.note: 'Countries Eligible for the JJWBGSP Scholarship in 2027' (World Bank brief, 15 Jul 2026), which matches Annex 1 of the 2027 Window 1 guidelines. The Window 2 guidelines' Annex 1 differs slightly: it adds Samoa and omits Namibia and Suriname. Samoa is kept here so Samoan applicants are not wrongly rejected; Namibia/Suriname applicants should confirm for Window 2 programs. 'West Bank and Gaza' is recorded as Palestine. Not eligible: dual citizens of a developed country, World Bank Group staff/EDs and their close relatives, current students of a participating program, and anyone who declined or did not finish an earlier JJ/WBGSP award. Not on the 2027 list, for example: Indonesia, Philippines, Vietnam, Sri Lanka, Jordan, Algeria. Japanese nationals have a separate track.

language.note: Set by your participating program; the admission letter must not be conditional on a language score.

field.note: Funding is only for the participating programs; your 3+ years of paid work must be development-related (Annex 2 lists suggested topics).

timeline.opening_month: January (Window 1 opens 18 Jan 2027); late March (Window 2 opens 29 Mar 2027)
timeline.typical_deadline: Window 1: 26 Feb 2027 (8 programs); Window 2: 21 May 2027, 12:00 noon EST (most programs)
timeline.result_announcement: Window 1: likely by end of March 2027; Window 2: likely by mid-July
timeline.course_start: Per the participating program (2027-2028 academic year)
timeline.university_offer_deadline: Unconditional admission letter (except for funding) must be uploaded before you submit the scholarship application

deadline.label: JJ/WBGSP Window 1 application (8 programs)

extra.label: JJ/WBGSP Window 2 application, 12:00 noon EST (most programs, e.g. LSE, Oxford, Leeds, SOAS, Tokyo, ANU, Erasmus, IHE Delft)

deadline.note: 2027 cycle (official program page and 2027 guidelines, updated Aug 2026): Window 1 18 Jan - 26 Feb 2027 (Brandeis, Columbia SIPA, Johns Hopkins MPH, KIT/VU Amsterdam, UC Berkeley MDP, Tsukuba, Williams, Yale Systemic Risk); Window 2 29 Mar - 21 May 2027 at 12:00 noon EST (all other participating programs). You must apply in the window of your program. The real first deadline is your university's admission deadline (often Dec-Feb), because the application link is sent only by the program to admitted, shortlisted applicants and you cannot submit without the unconditional admission letter. Submit at least a week early.

documents.label: Admission application to a JJ/WBGSP participating master's program (apply to the university first; it sends the scholarship form link to admitted, shortlisted applicants)
Unconditional (except for financing) letter of admission to the participating program for 2027-28, uploaded before you submit
documents.notes: Must be for a program outside your country of citizenship and residence. Offers conditional on transcripts or language scores are not accepted (see Annex 5).

documents.label: JJ/WBGSP online application form, one per person, in English or the program's language, including the Signature Page
Statement of Purpose questions in the application form (career plans and commitment to your home country's development)
Exactly two professional recommendations, submitted online by people who directly observed your paid development-related work (professors from your studies do not count)
documents.notes: Send the Recommendation Request Form before submitting the application; at least one from a current or former supervisor is suggested.

documents.label: Proof of 3+ years of paid development-related employment in the last 6 years (signed employer letters on letterhead; current-job letter dated within 3 months of the deadline)
documents.notes: Nationals of the fragile/conflict-affected countries in Annex 3 may document unpaid work or explain why proof is unavailable.

documents.label: Bachelor's diploma (and your most advanced graduate diploma, if any), with English translation if needed (uncertified translation accepted; do not upload transcripts instead)
CV in English or the program's language (Annex 4 format suggested; list only paid jobs as employment)
English (or teaching-language) proof required by your participating program, needed to get an unconditional admission
documents.notes: JJ/WBGSP sets no score itself.

documents.label: Passport identification page (finalists, within 3 business days of the scholarship offer)
Health certificate from a medical doctor (less than 3 months old at program start, due at least 21 days before travel)

application_portal_system: JJ/WBGSP online application (Zengine portal; link sent by the participating program to shortlisted admitted applicants; computer only, not phone)
strategic_tips: Work backwards from the university, not the World Bank: pick a participating program (check whether it is Window 1 or 2), meet its admission deadline and get an unconditional offer, because without it you cannot submit. Scoring is 30% professional experience, 30% professional recommendations, 30% commitment to your home country and 10% education, so document 3+ years of paid development work carefully and choose two supervisors who can describe your impact. Programs in your own country of citizenship or residence do not count.

name: Khalifa University Postgraduate Scholarships (MSc and PhD)
organization: Khalifa University of Science and Technology (Abu Dhabi)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: PhD scholarships may include a monthly stipend (general amount not published; the CSC-KU joint PhD pays AED 9,200/month); master's scholarship benefits do not list a stipend
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Depending on the award: full or partial tuition coverage, textbooks, accommodation, medical insurance, visa processing support and travel assistance to/from the UAE for students living abroad. PhD awards may add a monthly stipend, conference support and an international research internship (subject to funding) and teaching experience. Tuition otherwise: AED 5,000/credit hour (master's), AED 6,666/credit hour (doctoral).

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: UAE nationals and international students (all nationalities); merit-based and competitive. The CSC-KU joint PhD scholarship is only for citizens of the People's Republic of China.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Master's: bachelor's CGPA 3.0/4.0 (or UK upper second). Regular PhD: bachelor's 3.0 and master's 3.25. Direct PhD (no master's): bachelor's CGPA 3.5.
eligibility.language_requirements: TOEFL iBT 91 (test centre only, no Home Edition) or IELTS Academic 6.5 (EmSAT for UAE applicants). Waiver possible for native speakers, or for graduates of English-medium institutions who had IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL 79 when admitted to that degree.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Graduate programs in science, engineering, computing and health/medicine; awards weigh research potential and alignment with the University's strategic priorities.
eligibility.return_obligation: None

nationality.note: Scholarships are offered to UAE nationals and international students. The Combined Master-PhD Research Teaching Scholarship (CMDRTS) is for UAE nationals only; the CSC-KU joint PhD scholarship is for Chinese citizens only (deadline 10 February).

language.note: IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 91. An English-medium degree alone is not enough for a waiver: you also need proof of IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL 79 from your earlier admission.

field.note: Khalifa University's graduate programs are in science, engineering, computing and medicine/health; your bachelor's must be in a relevant discipline.

timeline.typical_deadline: March-April (Fall 2026: 2 Mar 2026, extended to 16 Mar 2026; Fall 2025: 14 Apr 2025)
timeline.interview_period: Admission interview after document review

deadline.label: KU postgraduate online application (Fall intake)
deadline.note: Fall 2026: the official page said applications 'close on 2 March 2026' (archived 31 Jan 2026), later 'open until 16 March 2026' (archived 11 Mar 2026). Fall 2025 window: 23 Dec 2024 - 14 Apr 2025. The Fall 2027 window is not announced yet (the page currently says Spring 2027 admissions are closed); expect it to open around December 2026 and close in March 2027. Start the UAE Ministry of Education degree equivalency early: it is required and slow.

documents.label: KU online postgraduate application (tick scholarship interest; AED 200 fee)
Certified copy of bachelor's/master's degree certificate
Equivalency / Recognition of University Certificates from the UAE Ministry of Education (for degrees from outside the UAE)
documents.notes: Lengthy process with attestation, notarisation and translation; start as soon as possible.

documents.label: Official transcript showing the grading scale
IELTS Academic 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 91 (test centre; TOEFL code 0960)
documents.notes: Upload evidence even if you request a waiver.

documents.label: GRE General (quantitative 150+, all three sections attempted; test centre only) for Direct PhD applicants; optional otherwise (GRE code 0822)
documents.notes: Mandatory only for Direct PhD (bachelor's to PhD).

documents.label: Detailed Curriculum Vitae
Statement of Purpose (500-1,000 words)
Research Statement (500-1,000 words), aligned with KU's institutional research priorities
At least two referee recommendations (submitted through the online form)
Passport-style photograph on a white background
Copy of valid passport (plus UAE visa and Emirates ID if you live in the UAE)

application_portal_system: Khalifa University online postgraduate admissions portal (scholarship interest indicated in the admission application)
strategic_tips: Indicate scholarship interest in the admission form: awards are decided with admission and weigh research potential and fit with KU's research priorities, so contact a faculty member in your target department and align your Research Statement with them. Begin the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency of your degree immediately, and book a test-centre IELTS/TOEFL (and GRE for Direct PhD). PhD scholarships are the most complete; master's awards may not include a stipend.

name: KNB Scholarship (Kemitraan Negara Berkembang / Developing Countries Partnership)
organization: Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Technology of Indonesia (Directorate of Institutional Affairs, DG Higher Education), with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Monthly living allowance plus monthly research and book allowance (amounts not published on the official site)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Settlement allowance on arrival; tuition for the Indonesian language year (BIPA) and the academic program (regular class, not international class); monthly living and research/book allowances while in Indonesia; health insurance (outpatient, inpatient, accidents); one-time funding to publish a scientific article (Master's and PhD); economy return airfare plus local transport. Dormitories depend on the university. Duration: up to 12 months BIPA + 24 months Master's / 48 months PhD or Bachelor. No support for family members.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Foreign nationals from developing countries or countries with bilateral relations with Indonesia; the country list is set on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' recommendation. Indonesians, refugees and stateless persons cannot apply. A recommendation letter from the Indonesian Embassy/Consulate General for your country of origin is mandatory.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Minimum GPA 2.75 for Bachelor's and 3.00 for Master's and Doctoral levels (FAQ).
eligibility.language_requirements: Master's: TOEFL ITP 500 / iBT 61, IELTS 6.0, TOEIC 575; PhD: TOEFL ITP 530 / iBT 71, IELTS 6.0, TOEIC 640; Bachelor's: TOEFL ITP 477 / iBT 53, IELTS 5.5, TOEIC 510 (or equivalent such as Duolingo; taken in the last 2 years). Exempt for nationals of English-speaking countries or graduates of English-taught programs (official proof). All studies are taught in Indonesian after a compulsory Indonesian language year (BIPA).
eligibility.age_limit: Maximum age on 31 December 2026: 21 for Bachelor's, 35 for Master's, 40 for Doctorate (2026 call). The system filters out applicants over the limit.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Programs at the 47 KNB host universities (about 1,173 study programs, listed in the guideline annex); the program must match your previous degree. You cannot apply for a level you already hold.
eligibility.return_obligation: Must return to your home country within 60 days after the program ends; no marriage to Indonesian citizens/permanent residents or other scholars and no pregnancy during the scholarship.

nationality.note: KNB has no published 'eligible countries' list: it is for developing countries or countries with bilateral relations, and home countries are chosen on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' recommendation (FAQ). The countries above are those in the 'Annex of Indonesian Representative' of the KNB Scholarship 2026 Guideline (the embassy/consulate that issues your recommendation letter for 116 numbered entries), so they are very likely covered; any other nationality should confirm with the nearest Indonesian Embassy. The recommendation must come from the Indonesian mission for your country of origin, not your country of residence. Refugees and stateless persons are not eligible.

language.note: IELTS 6.0 for Master's/PhD (5.5 for Bachelor's) or equivalent TOEFL/TOEIC/Duolingo within the last 2 years; exempt with official proof of an English-taught degree or English-speaking nationality. Classes are in Indonesian after a compulsory BIPA language year.

field.note: Choose a program aligned with your previous degree; no matriculation is offered for unrelated fields.

timeline.typical_deadline: 31 March (2026/2027 call: 2 Feb - 31 Mar 2026)
timeline.interview_period: May (online interviews and psychological tests by the universities: 4-22 May 2026)
timeline.course_start: Arrival late August; BIPA Indonesian language program starts September

deadline.label: KNB online application (needs the Indonesian Embassy recommendation letter first)
deadline.note: 2026/2027 schedule (official site and 2026 guideline): applications 2 Feb - 31 Mar 2026; embassy verification 6-17 Apr; ministry verification 20-30 Apr; academic selection, interviews and psychotests 4-22 May; announcement 19 Jun; re-registration 22-26 Jun; visa documents 20 Jul - 21 Aug; arrival 24-31 Aug; BIPA from Sep 2026. The 2027/2028 call is not announced yet; expect a similar Feb-March window. The Indonesian Embassy recommendation (with verification and an interview) must be obtained before you submit, so contact the embassy in January.

documents.label: Recommendation letter for the KNB scholarship from the Indonesian Embassy or Consulate General of your country of origin (current selection year)
documents.notes: Submit the KNB Offering Letter, passport, CV, English test, recommendation letters, certificates/transcripts and medical report to the embassy; it verifies you (background/security check and interview). Honorary consuls cannot issue it.

documents.label: KNB online application form (knb.kemdiktisaintek.go.id), with a YouTube link to a video of max 5 minutes (your profile, why Indonesia and KNB, why this campus and program)
Official (non-diplomatic) passport valid until at least 31 December 2027
Curriculum vitae in English or Bahasa Indonesia
English test (Master's: TOEFL ITP 500/iBT 61, IELTS 6.0, TOEIC 575; PhD: TOEFL ITP 530/iBT 71, IELTS 6.0, TOEIC 640; Bachelor's: IELTS 5.5) taken within 2 years
Recommendation letter from your employer/immediate supervisor (or a statement letter if unemployed), in English or Bahasa
Academic recommendation letter from your previous school, signed by the head of the institution, in English or Bahasa
Bachelor's (for Master's) or Master's (for PhD) degree certificate in English or Bahasa, legalized by your Ministry of Education and Ministry of Foreign Affairs
High-school certificate in English or Bahasa, legalized by your Ministry of Education and Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Academic transcript of the previous degree in English or Bahasa, legalized by your Ministry of Education and Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Certified medical report issued within the last 3 months: physical exam, TB, syphilis, HIV/AIDS, Ebola and Mpox tests, mental health test and negative drug test
documents.notes: Yellow fever vaccination certificate also required if you come from or live in Africa.

documents.label: Recommendation letter from a potential research supervisor at your chosen KNB host university (same university you apply to)
Statement of purpose with dissertation proposal: purpose of study, why Indonesia and your research topic, academic plans (English or Bahasa)
Student Agreement signed at re-registration (no marriage to Indonesians/other scholars, no pregnancy, no military service, return home within 60 days)

application_portal_system: KNB Scholarship online system (knb.kemdiktisaintek.go.id) after obtaining the Indonesian Embassy recommendation
strategic_tips: Start with the Indonesian Embassy in January: its recommendation (with verification and an interview) is mandatory and takes time, and your degree documents must be legalized by your education and foreign ministries. Pick a host university and program from the 2026 guideline annex that matches your previous degree, because you cannot change it later. Expect a full year of Indonesian (BIPA) before classes, which are taught in Indonesian, and mind the strict age cut-offs (35 for Master's, 40 for PhD on 31 December).

name: Malaysia International Scholarship (MIS)
organization: Ministry of Higher Education Malaysia (MOHE), Scholarship Division

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: RM 1,500/month living allowance (paid every 4 months on submission of a progress report)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Tuition fees for the whole sponsorship period are paid directly to the university. The 2026 guidelines list no airfare, insurance, housing or visa benefits; scholars must arrange their own visa (including a medical exam).

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Citizens of the MIS 2026 recipient countries: ASEAN countries, Commonwealth countries, and 39 named countries (e.g. Afghanistan, Algeria, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Morocco, Palestine, Saudi Arabia, Sudan, Syria, Turkiye, Yemen, China, Japan, South Korea, Russia, Brazil, Chile). Also open to current full-time postgraduates at a participating Malaysian institution with at least two semesters left.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Master's: CGPA 3.00 or 2nd Class Upper (Honours) in the bachelor's degree. PhD: CGPA 3.00 / excellent results in a related master's degree.
eligibility.language_requirements: IELTS 6.0, TOEFL PBT 550 (or equivalent), or an official university declaration that your previous degree was taught in English.
eligibility.age_limit: Not more than 40 (Master's) or 45 (PhD) at the time of application.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Any accredited course at the 24 participating universities, with priority to education, arts and humanities, social sciences, business/administration/law, natural sciences, ICT, engineering, agriculture and health (excluding medicine, nursing and pharmacy). Full-time study only.
eligibility.return_obligation: None stated

nationality.note: 'Recipient Countries of MIS 2026' from the official 2026 guidelines: ASEAN (Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam), 'Commonwealth countries (CPA regions of Africa, Asia, Australia, British Islands & Mediterranean, Canada, the Caribbean, Americas & the Atlantic, India and the Pacific)', which is expanded here to the Commonwealth member states (small territories such as Jersey, Guernsey or Isle of Man are not listed), and 39 named countries. Not listed, for example: United States, most EU countries, Ethiopia, Mali, Somalia, Lebanon, Nepal, Mongolia, Argentina, Mexico. The 2027 list is not published yet; re-verify.

language.note: IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL PBT 550, or an official declaration from your university that your degree was taught in English.

field.note: Priority areas cover almost all fields; medicine, nursing and pharmacy are excluded from the health area.

timeline.opening_month: Varies: March in 2026 (4 Mar), June in 2025 (10 Jun)

name: Schwarzman Scholars
organization: Schwarzman Scholars, Schwarzman College, Tsinghua University (Beijing)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Personal stipend (amount not published on the official site)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Tuition and fees, room and board, travel to and from Beijing at the start and end of the academic year, an in-country study tour, health insurance and a personal stipend (the FAQ also lists a laptop). Visa costs are not mentioned.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: All nationalities. Class targets: about 40% United States, 20% China and 40% rest of the world. Holders of Chinese passports or permanent resident cards (Mainland, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan) apply through a separate China application system with an earlier deadline.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No minimum GPA or class rank; the most competitive applicants are at the top of their graduating class.
eligibility.language_requirements: If English is not your native language: TOEFL iBT 100 (or 5 on the 6-point scale), IELTS 7, Cambridge C1 Advanced / C2 Proficiency 185 or Duolingo 130. Waived if you studied at least two years of your undergraduate program, or two or more years at master's level or higher, in English.
eligibility.age_limit: At least 18 and not yet 29 on 1 August of the enrollment year (1 August 2027 for the Class of 2027-2028; 1 August 2028 for the Class of 2028-2029).
eligibility.field_restrictions: Any undergraduate field. One-year master's degree and leadership program at Tsinghua University (core curriculum in Global Affairs, China and Leadership, plus electives).
eligibility.return_obligation: None

nationality.note: Open to all nationalities. Applicants with Chinese citizenship (Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan) use the separate China Application System (Schwarzman College admissions page) and apply January-May 20 instead of April-September. Applicants who already hold a graduate degree may apply.

language.note: Waived after two or more years of English-taught undergraduate study or two or more years of English-taught master's-level (or higher) study. Some tests are valid for only two years.

timeline.result_announcement: End of the October-November selection cycle; applicants with Chinese citizenship before July

items: Leadership essay with specific examples of your leadership

name: Yenching Academy of Peking University (Yenching Scholars)
organization: Yenching Academy, Peking University (Beijing)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Monthly stipend (amount not published on the official site)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: First-year Yenching Fellowship: tuition, a room in the Yenching Academy House, a travel stipend for one round trip between a base city in your country of nationality and Beijing, basic medical insurance, a monthly stipend and research/field-study costs. A second-year fellowship (tuition, housing support, insurance, stipend) is available only if you keep good standing and stay in Beijing. Visa costs are not mentioned.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: International applicants must be non-Chinese citizens with a valid passport. Applicants from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan apply through the same portal plus a Peking University supplementary application. Mainland Chinese applicants use a separate Peking University process (only for current undergraduates at Mainland universities).
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Outstanding academic record (no numeric minimum published).
eligibility.language_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0, TOEFL iBT 100 or Cambridge English Scale 185, taken after 1 Sept 2025 and sent directly to the Academy (TOEFL code C488; no TOEFL Home Edition, MyBest, IELTS Online/Indicator). Not required for native English speakers or graduates of an English-taught degree.
eligibility.age_limit: No strict cut-off, but no one over 29 has been admitted (except Zhuoyue Scholarship recipients); average entry age is 23.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Any undergraduate field. Two-year interdisciplinary Master's in China Studies; scholars choose one of six research areas (Economics and Management; History and Archaeology; Philosophy and Religion; Politics and International Relations; Law and Society; Literature and Culture).
eligibility.return_obligation: None

nationality.note: International track: non-Chinese citizens with a valid passport (former Chinese citizens need passports/citizenship documents dated before 30 April 2021 plus proof of cancelled Chinese nationality). Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan applicants use the YCA portal plus a Peking University supplementary application. Mainland Chinese applicants follow a separate Peking University process and must be current undergraduates at a Mainland university. Students and alumni of YCA partner universities must first pass their home university's internal pre-selection.

language.note: Exempt if English is your native language or you graduated from an English-taught degree program (international applicants). Tests must be taken after 1 Sept 2025.

field.note: All undergraduate fields are welcome, but the degree is China Studies in the humanities and social sciences; you must show a strong interest in studying China.

timeline.typical_deadline: 30 November, 9:00 a.m. Beijing time (2027 cohort)
timeline.interview_period: Winter or early spring (online for international finalists; in person at Peking University for Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan applicants)
timeline.result_announcement: Around April; final admission confirmed by the Peking University acceptance letter in the summer

Students and alumni of partner universities must go through their university's internal pre-selection first, which usually has an earlier internal deadline. Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan applicants also have a Peking University supplementary application.

Personal statement (750 words or less)

name: Becas Chile – Doctorate Abroad (Doctorado Becas Chile, ANID)
organization: Agencia Nacional de Investigación y Desarrollo (ANID), Government of Chile

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Monthly maintenance set per destination country/city in Annex II of the bases (e.g. Germany US$1,562, Australia US$1,556, Belgium US$1,596), plus family allowances for spouse and children
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Round-trip economy airfare (also for spouse/civil partner and children), tuition and enrolment fees, installation allowance US$500, books and materials US$300/year, health insurance US$800/year, return allowance US$500, maternity extension of maintenance, visa costs, and support for English/German/French levelling courses. Up to 4 years (48 months) from programme entry.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Chilean citizens or foreigners with permanent residence (residencia definitiva) in Chile
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Academic excellence: undergraduate average of at least 5.0 on the Chilean 1–7 scale (or equivalent), OR being in the top 30% of your graduating cohort
eligibility.language_requirements: No minimum score to apply. Applicants to programmes taught in English, German or French without an unconditional acceptance must submit language certificates (max 2 years old) used to classify their level for levelling courses; an unconditional acceptance letter or regular-student certificate counts as proof of language.
eligibility.field_restrictions: All fields, with selection focused on the priority areas defined by the Ministry of Science. Full-time, in-person, daytime programmes entirely abroad (any country except Chile); online or part-time programmes are excluded. Applicants must already be accepted or enrolled as regular students.
eligibility.return_obligation: Return to Chile within 4 years after the scholarship ends and stay for twice the scholarship duration (Santiago Metropolitan Region residents) or the same duration (residents of other regions).

nationality.note: Chileans, or foreigners holding a valid permanent residence in Chile (certificate issued on or after 1 July 2025 required). Study must take place outside Chile.

language.note: ANID sets no minimum; the host university's admission rules apply. Applicants with a language-conditional offer submit certificates (e.g. IELTS, TOEFL, Duolingo, Goethe, DELF) at most 2 years old, used to place them in funded levelling courses.

field.note: All areas of knowledge; evaluation favours ministry priority areas and institutions in the top 100 of ANID's ranking per OECD sub-area.

timeline.typical_deadline: Mid/late May (2026: 15 April – 19 May 2026)
timeline.course_start: Any start date accepted by the host programme (must already be accepted or enrolled)

deadline.label: Doctorado Becas Chile application (ANID online system)

The Master's abroad call (Magíster Becas Chile) last ran 9 April – 13 May 2025; ChileAtiende lists no Magíster call for 2026, so Master's is left out of this record until a new call appears.
