deadline.note: 2026-2027 round: 'Application Deadlines: March 15, 2026' (AIMS Ghana post of 15 Dec 2025, same date on AIMS Cameroon). Previous rounds closed 21 Mar 2025 (AIMS Rwanda) and 29 Mar 2024. The 2027-28 call was not yet published on 25 Oct 2026. AIMS South Africa also runs a January intake for South African applicants only (applications August-October).

documents.label: Online application form (AIMS network application portal, apply.aims-network.org; AIMS South Africa: apply.aims.ac.za)
Undergraduate and postgraduate transcripts
Degree certificate (or proof you will graduate before the programme starts)
documents.notes: Not listed on the AIMS South Africa page but needed to prove the 4-year degree; confirm on the portal.

documents.label: CV
Cover letter
Sample work

application_portal_system: AIMS network online application (one application, centre preference chosen in the form); AIMS South Africa uses apply.aims.ac.za
strategic_tips: One application covers the AIMS centres (South Africa, Senegal, Ghana, Cameroon, Rwanda), so apply early in the January-March window and show strong mathematics plus concrete leadership and community-service examples. Prepare your sample work and cover letter in advance and expect an online interview. If you once held an AIMS scholarship you cannot apply again.
program_status_note: 2026-2027 cohort admitted (e.g. 44 students at AIMS South Africa); the 2027-2028 call is expected around December 2026 - March 2027 but is not yet published. Referee requirements are not stated on the official pages - check the portal.

name: Moroccan Government Scholarships for Foreign Students (AMCI - Agence Marocaine de Coopération Internationale)
organization: Moroccan Agency for International Cooperation (AMCI), Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Morocco, with the Ministry of Higher Education and partner-country ministries

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: AMCI monthly scholarship (amount not published on the official pages consulted)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Places at Moroccan public higher-education institutions (and, for vocational training, at OFPPT or agricultural institutes) with an AMCI scholarship. AMCI scholars can be housed at the Cité Universitaire Internationale in Rabat (on-site clinic); the Centre International de Langues offers French upgrade and Darija courses. Official pages do not state the stipend amount or whether fees, travel or housing are paid; the Benin call requires the student to buy health insurance in Morocco and the family to send a monthly top-up of 50,000 FCFA, so treat it as a partial award.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Nationals of countries that have a cooperation agreement with Morocco and receive an annual AMCI quota (mainly African countries); applications only through the diplomatic channel / home ministry
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Set by each partner country's call. Example (Benin 2026-27): Baccalaureate of the current/previous year with mention 'Très Bien', 'Bien' or 'Assez Bien' for undergraduate places; mention 'Bien' for Master's.
eligibility.language_requirements: French is the teaching language of Moroccan public higher-education institutions; non-francophone students can take French upgrade courses at AMCI's Centre International de Langues.
eligibility.age_limit: Set per country and per field (Benin 2026-27: 'respecter les critères d'âge selon les filières'; Benin 2025-26 horticulture technician call: 30 or younger on 1 September)
eligibility.field_restrictions: You study in the field/programme allocated by the Moroccan side from the list offered to your country (e.g. engineering prep classes, engineering, medicine, nursing, architecture, management, tourism, agronomy; vocational: specialised technician programmes at OFPPT or the Agadir horticulture complex).
eligibility.return_obligation: None stated by AMCI (home-country rules may apply)

nationality.note: No public country list. AMCI grants an annual quota to each partner country (e.g. Benin: 80 university scholarships for 2026-27); 'Les étudiants étrangers présenteront nécessairement leur candidature par voie diplomatique' and files not forwarded by AMCI are not considered. Moroccan nationals are not eligible. Check with your Ministry of Higher Education / scholarships directorate or the Moroccan embassy.

language.note: French-medium teaching; no level is stated. AMCI's Centre International de Langues runs French courses and issues an 'attestation de réussite' for further study.

field.note: Fields are offered per country each year and the Moroccan side assigns the programme.

timeline.opening_month: Around May-June (national calls by each partner country; Benin's 2025 calls were posted on 2 June 2025 with a 12 June deadline)
timeline.typical_deadline: May to July, set by each country's ministry (Benin: 12 June 2026 for 2026-27 university places; 12 June 2025 for 2025-26 vocational places)
timeline.result_announcement: Not published (placements are decided by the Moroccan Ministry of Higher Education via AMCI)

deadline.label: National deadline of your ministry / Moroccan embassy (example: Benin)
deadline.note: Each partner country runs its own call and deadline before forwarding files to AMCI. Benin (official communiqué, 2026-27): 80 scholarships, deadline Friday 12 June 2026 at 12:00; Benin 2025-26 vocational (OFPPT) and horticulture technician calls: 12 June 2025. Other countries' dates (May-July 2026) were seen only on news/aggregator sites. The 2027-28 calls are expected around April-June 2027.

documents.label: Moroccan scholarship application form (formulaire de demande de bourse marocaine) from your ministry, completed and signed
Certified copy of the Baccalaureate certificate (or school certificate + final-year reports if the bac is pending)
Certified copy of transcripts (Bac transcript; for Master/PhD all transcripts from the Bac to the last university year)
Certified copies of university diplomas / attestations (Licence, Master...)
Copy of the study programmes (syllabi) of the degrees obtained
Master's dissertation (mémoire)
Doctoral thesis project (projet de thèse)
Copy of the (secure) birth certificate or equivalent
Copy of the certificate of nationality (certificat de nationalité)
Copy of passport or biometric identity card
Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) less than 3 months old
Original medical certificate from a sworn doctor: no serious, transmissible or contagious disease (notably tuberculosis)
Certificate of authenticity and equivalence for diplomas obtained abroad
Application and motivation letter to the institute director stating the chosen programme (asked in some vocational calls, e.g. Agadir horticulture technician)

application_portal_system: Paper/online file submitted to your own Ministry of Higher Education (scholarships directorate) or the Moroccan embassy, which forwards selected files to AMCI
strategic_tips: Watch your own ministry's scholarship page from April: the Moroccan offer is announced country by country with a short deadline and a fixed list of programmes and places. Prepare the certified Bac and transcripts, birth and nationality certificates, police record (under 3 months) and medical certificate in advance. Teaching is in French, so non-francophones should plan for AMCI's French course; vocational places (specialised technician, Bac+2 at OFPPT or agricultural institutes) are offered in some years.
program_status_note: Diploma level verified: partner-country calls for 2025-26 offered vocational 'Technicien Spécialisé' (Bac+2) places at OFPPT and at the Complexe Horticole d'Agadir under AMCI scholarships (Benin DBAU). A separate 'BTS' track was not found on official pages. The AMCI stipend amount is not published on the official pages consulted (older unofficial sources cite 750 MAD/month - unverified).

name: DAAD In-Country/In-Region Scholarship Programme Sub-Saharan Africa
country: Sub-Saharan Africa (host universities in the region)
organization: German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD), funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Set per host institution in each call (2027 intake): In-Country EUR 300-400/month, In-Region EUR 400-500/month (e.g. University of Rwanda: 300 In-Country / 400 In-Region; Chuka University, Ardhi University, UDS Ghana: 400 / 500)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Tuition fees paid directly to the host university (amount in the Letter of Award); study and research allowance EUR 460/year; thesis publishing costs EUR 400 (once). Travel allowance and health insurance are paid to In-Region scholars ONLY (In-Country scholars get neither). Holders in research-based Master's may apply for a 3-6 month research stay in Germany (subject to funds). The monthly payment is meant to cover accommodation and food.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Graduates from Sub-Saharan Africa: nationals or permanent residents of a Sub-Saharan African country (49 countries on the DAAD list)
eligibility.gpa_requirement: First academic degree (3- or 4-year Bachelor or equivalent) with above-average results: at least Second Class/Upper Division or equivalent (some calls also state a cumulative average of at least 70%). Candidates without Second Class Upper are not eligible.
eligibility.language_requirements: Thorough knowledge of the language of instruction of the chosen programme (no test score set by DAAD; host universities may ask for proof). All documents uploaded to the DAAD portal must be in English or German.
eligibility.age_limit: No age limit, but the last university degree must have been completed no more than 6 years before the time of application.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Only the development-related Master's programmes at the selected host institutions (2027 intake: water and environmental engineering, seed science, molecular cell biology of infectious diseases, agricultural economics, environmental health, plant breeding, education in research, electrical power systems, geomatics, climate change and disaster management, aquaculture and fisheries, irrigation engineering; earlier round: urban studies, mathematics, physics).
eligibility.return_obligation: None formal, but the programme targets people planning a career in teaching and/or research at a higher education institution in Sub-Saharan Africa (university staff and public-sector candidates first).

nationality.note: Country list from the DAAD scholarship database entry (Sub-Saharan Africa). The calls say applicants 'must be nationals or permanent residents of a Sub-Saharan African country', so permanent residents of these countries also qualify. In-Country = study in your home country or the country where you hold a residence permit; In-Region = study in another Sub-Saharan country. Some calls exclude a group: e.g. the UCT (South Africa) call is In-Region only and closed to South African citizens and permanent residents. Refugees with recognised status are especially encouraged. Previous DAAD Master's scholarship holders are not eligible.

language.note: 'Thorough knowledge of the language of instruction' - no IELTS/TOEFL minimum is set by DAAD; programmes are mostly taught in English (2iE Burkina Faso may also use French). Check the host university's admission rules.

field.note: Only the listed Master's programmes at DAAD partner institutions; each call names one programme and its admission background.

timeline.opening_month: August to September (calls for the 2027 intake were published in August 2026); a second group of calls is published in spring
timeline.typical_deadline: DAAD portal: 12 November 2026 for the calls currently open for the 2027 intake (24:00 CET). An earlier round for the 2027 intake closed 29 April 2026 (e.g. UCT, South Africa). Host universities set their own admission deadlines.
timeline.interview_period: Selection usually April to September (interviews possible)
timeline.result_announcement: About six months after the application deadline
timeline.course_start: August to November 2027 depending on the host (scholarship usually begins 1 August, 1 September, 1 October or 1 November)

deadline.label: DAAD portal deadline (most host institutions); apply to the host university separately

extra.label: Earlier round of calls (2027 intake: DAAD fact sheet deadline 29 Apr 2026, e.g. UCT MPhil Urban Studies)

deadline.note: Deadlines are set per call. All 13 calls currently linked from the DAAD database (2iE Burkina Faso; WACCI, WACCBIP and UDS Ghana; Jimma Ethiopia; Chuka and Moi Kenya; University of Rwanda; Ardhi Tanzania; Busitema Uganda; MUBAS and LUANAR x2 Malawi) close on 12 Nov 2026 at 24:00 CET for the 2027 intake. An earlier round also aimed at the 2027 intake closed on 29 Apr 2026 (DAAD 2027 fact sheet listing Burkina Faso, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda; UCT MPhil Urban Studies call on africancentreforcities.net). DAAD now lists FUNAAB (Nigeria), UCT and UP (South Africa) as calls to be published in spring 2027. The host university's own admission deadline can be earlier - check each call.

documents.label: Online application form in the DAAD Portal (portal.meindaad.de), fully completed and submitted
Curriculum Vitae in tabular form
DAAD form Letter of Recommendation, completed, signed and (if possible) stamped by a university teacher
documents.notes: Only the DAAD recommendation form is accepted.

documents.label: Copy of the most recent Bachelor's / university degree certificate including final grades (final certificate only - no provisional certificates)
documents.notes: Add the grading scale and, if available, information on recognition of the degree in the host country. Non-English/German documents need a certified translation.

documents.label: Transcript of Records of the most recent university degree
Letter of Motivation, 1-2 pages (300-1000 words): personal, social and academic motivation plus a possible Master's project; rank your choices if applying to more than one programme (max. 3)
Copy of a valid passport or national identity card
Separate application for admission to the host university, using its own procedure and deadline
documents.notes: DAAD only reviews the DAAD portal application; admission and the university's pre-selection ranking are done by the host.

documents.label: Recognition/equivalence document from the host country's qualifications authority, where required (mainly In-Region applicants)
Proof of Admission from the host university (may be uploaded later, before the scholarship begins)
Semester schedule (course-based Master's) and/or time schedule / workplan (research-based Master's)
documents.notes: Must be uploaded no later than the start of scholarship funding.

documents.label: Additional documents (e.g. proof of employment or internships), list of publications, refugee ID / UNHCR registration if applicable

application_portal_system: DAAD Portal (portal.meindaad.de, one funding-programme link per call) PLUS the host university's own admission application
strategic_tips: You must apply twice: in the DAAD Portal by the call deadline (12 Nov 2026 for most 2027 calls) and to the host university under its own admission rules and deadline. Only programmes at the listed partner universities are funded, so read the call for your target programme (background degree, Second Class Upper, degree not older than 6 years). If you apply to several programmes (max. 3), rank them in your motivation letter, and get the mandatory DAAD recommendation form to your lecturer early.
program_status_note: Calls for the 2027 intake are open (DAAD portal deadline 12 Nov 2026). The current calls are Master's only; no PhD calls are listed in the DAAD database entry. Host institutions change from cycle to cycle.

name: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS-U) - Associate Degree Program (University Track)
organization: National Institute for International Education (NIIED), Ministry of Education, Republic of Korea

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Korean language program: 13,560,000 KRW per year; degree program: 14,400,000 KRW per year (about 1,130,000 / 1,200,000 KRW per month)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Tuition: NIIED pays up to 5 million KRW and the university covers any amount above that plus the admission fee. Korean language program fee 5.2 million KRW per year. Economy-class flight ticket (actual cost; not for scholars already in Korea or entering from a third country). The monthly allowance is 'all-inclusive': living expenses, accommodation, health insurance, Korean proficiency grants, TOPIK fee, settlement allowance and degree completion grant are paid out of it (no separate housing or insurance payment).

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Citizens of the 74 NIIED-designated countries invited to the 2027 GKS-U program (associate degree: 30 scholars from 74 countries); applicants and their parents must not hold Korean citizenship
eligibility.gpa_requirement: High-school CGPA of 80% or above, OR top 20% of the class, OR CGPA at least 2.64/4.0 (2.80/4.3, 2.91/4.5, 3.23/5.0)
eligibility.language_requirements: No mandatory test; TOPIK (original) or an English test (copy) can be submitted if available. One year of Korean language training is included (TOPIK 5-6 holders are exempt). Each college may set its own requirements.
eligibility.age_limit: Under 25 (born after 1 March 2002 for the 2027 program)
eligibility.field_restrictions: Any associate-degree department listed by the 9 participating colleges in the 'University Information' file (night, short-term, online and distance programs excluded)
eligibility.return_obligation: None

nationality.note: The 74 countries of the 2027 GKS-U quota table ('Associate Degree: 30 scholars from 74 countries'; same 74 as the Embassy Track General program). Separately, the UIC (University-Industry Cooperation) program - which includes associate degrees in electrical/mechanical engineering and software at Dong-Eui Institute of Technology, Kyungbok University and Osan University - is open to ALL countries. Applicants with dual Korean citizenship (or whose parent has it) are not eligible; former GKS degree scholars cannot apply.

language.note: Korean language training (1 year) is included; TOPIK or English scores add value but are optional at NIIED level.

field.note: Only associate-degree departments at the 9 participating colleges; apply to ONE college and ONE department.

timeline.opening_month: September (guidelines published September; University Track applications September to November)
timeline.typical_deadline: September to November, set by each participating college (University Track); applications must reach NIIED by 30 November
timeline.interview_period: College first-round selection in November (no third round on the University Track)
timeline.result_announcement: NIIED second round by mid-December; final GKS-U scholars announced about 7 January
timeline.course_start: Korean language program from early 2027 (one year), then the degree program from March 2028 (TOPIK 5-6 holders start the degree in March 2027)

deadline.label: Participating college's own GKS associate-degree deadline (University Track)
deadline.note: 2027 GKS-U guideline (Sept 2026, attached to the Korean Embassy in Kenya notice): University Track 'Application Period: September-November 2026, according to each university's own schedule'; successful first-round files arrive at NIIED by 30 Nov 2026; final announcement expected 7 Jan 2027. Some college deadlines for the 2027 program may still be open in late Oct/Nov 2026 - check each college's announcement. Embassy-track failures (results by 16 Oct) may still apply to the University Track.

documents.label: (Form 1) Application Form, written in English
(Form 2) Personal Statement (English or Korean)
(Form 3) Study Plan (English or Korean)
(Form 4) Recommendation Letter (original letter from the recommender)
(Form 5) GKS Applicant Agreement and (Form 7) Consent to Collect and Use Personal Information, signed
(Form 6) Personal Medical Assessment
Proof of citizenship of the applicant and parents and proof of family relationship
High school graduation certificate (or certificate of expected graduation)
documents.notes: Apostille or consular confirmation; non-English/Korean documents need a certified translation.

documents.label: Academic transcript of the high school curriculum
Valid TOPIK score report (original) or English proficiency test (copy), if you have one
Copies of awards and other certificates (up to 5, from high school onward)
Applicant's passport
Any additional documents required by the chosen college, submitted by its own method (in person, by mail, etc.)

application_portal_system: University Track: apply directly to ONE participating college by its own method and deadline (not the Study in Korea online system used by the Embassy Track)
strategic_tips: This is a University Track program: pick ONE of the 9 participating colleges and ONE department and follow that college's own call (usually September-November). Start apostilles early for your high-school certificate, transcript and family/citizenship documents, since they are required for NIIED's second round. You cannot also apply to the UIC program or another GKS track in the same year.
program_status_note: Confirmed in the 2027 GKS-U guidelines (Sept 2026): Associate Degree program, 30 scholars from 74 countries, at Busan Institute of Science and Technology, Cheju Halla University, Dong-Eui Institute of Technology, Induk University, Korea University of Media Arts, Kyungbok University, Kyung-In Women's University, Kyungnam College of Information & Technology and Yeungnam University College. Scholarship period 3-4 years (1 year Korean language + 2-3 years degree).

name: ICTP Postgraduate Diploma Programme (pre-PhD), Trieste
organization: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP), UNESCO / IAEA / Government of Italy

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Living expenses in Trieste for the full year are covered for scholarship holders (amount not published on the official page)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: The programme is tuition-free. About 10 scholarships per subject area each year for applicants from developing countries, covering travel and living expenses during the stay. Accommodation and health insurance are not described on the official page. Non-scholarship students may attend at their own cost.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Citizens of UN, UNESCO or IAEA member states; scholarships go to students from developing countries, with emphasis on the least developed regions
eligibility.gpa_requirement: A degree equivalent to an MSc (or an exceptionally good BSc) in physics, mathematics or a related field; selection on university performance and academic recommendations
eligibility.language_requirements: English: 'fluency in speaking and writing is an essential qualification'; proof of ability to follow advanced courses in English is required (no test score set)
eligibility.age_limit: Generally below 28 years of age
eligibility.field_restrictions: Five areas: High Energy, Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics; Condensed Matter Physics; Earth System Physics; Mathematics; Quantitative Life Sciences
eligibility.return_obligation: None stated

nationality.note: Anyone from a UN/UNESCO/IAEA member state may apply, but the scholarships are for students from developing countries. ICTP does not publish its developing-country list on the programme page; the OECD DAC list is used here as the closest proxy - check with diploma@ictp.it if your country is borderline.

language.note: Proof of English ability is required, but no IELTS/TOEFL minimum is published.

field.note: Applicants need a physics, mathematics or closely related degree.

timeline.opening_month: Early in the year (the 2025 and 2026 calls were in ICTP news in February, with online Q&A sessions in late February)
timeline.typical_deadline: Late February to mid-March (2026-27: poster 28 Feb 2026, extended to 15 Mar 2026; 2025-26: 15 Mar 2025)
timeline.course_start: 1 September (programme runs 1 Sep - 31 Aug in Trieste)

deadline.label: ICTP e-applications (Postgraduate Diploma call)
deadline.note: 2026-2027 call: the official poster gave 28 Feb 2026 and ICTP then announced the deadline 'has been extended to 15 March 2026'. The 2025-2026 call closed 15 Mar 2025. The programme page shows the 2027-2028 call as 'To be announced' (25 Oct 2026). The pattern date uses the earlier, original deadline to be safe.

documents.label: Online application form (ICTP e-applications)
Transcripts in English (originals or certified copies required later for selected candidates)
Degree certificate(s) in English (originals or certified copies required later for selected candidates)
Proof of ability to follow advanced courses and write in English
Two letters of recommendation from senior scientists

application_portal_system: ICTP e-applications portal (e-applications.ictp.it)
strategic_tips: The Diploma is a one-year, PhD-preparation year: the strongest applicants already hold an MSc (an exceptional BSc is also considered) and are under 28. Your two recommendation letters from senior scientists carry great weight, so ask referees who know your research or advanced coursework, and apply to the one subject area that matches your degree. Watch ICTP news from January: deadlines have been late February to mid-March and are sometimes extended.
program_status_note: 2026-2027 cohort selected; 2027-2028 call 'To be announced' on the official page as of 25 Oct 2026.

name: MEXT Japanese Government Scholarship - College of Technology (KOSEN) and Specialized Training College (Senshu) Students
organization: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Government of Japan - Embassy Recommendation

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: 117,000 JPY/month (+2,000 or 3,000 JPY regional supplement in designated areas; may change with the budget)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees waived at the preparatory institution and the KOSEN / specialized training college. Economy round-trip air ticket (to Japan on arrival, home after graduation). The guidelines do not mention health insurance or housing - these are paid from the allowance.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Nationals of countries that have diplomatic relations with Japan (Japanese nationals not eligible; dual nationals must give up Japanese nationality by arrival)
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No minimum grade in the guidelines; selection by documents, written exams and interview at the Japanese embassy
eligibility.language_requirements: Willingness to learn Japanese and to study in Japanese (all classes are in Japanese; a 1-year preparatory course is included). Written first-screening exams include Japanese and English. A JLPT/English certificate is optional.
eligibility.age_limit: Born on or after 2 April 2002 (for April 2027 arrival), i.e. under 25. Specialized Training College applicants qualifying through an equivalency exam must be 18+ at admission.
eligibility.field_restrictions: KOSEN: (A) Mechanical, (B) Electrical and Electronic, (C) Information, Communication and Network, (D) Materials Engineering, (E) Architecture, (F) Civil, (G) Maritime Engineering, (H) Other (international communication, management information engineering). Specialized Training College: (A) Technology, (B) Personal Care and Nutrition, (C) Education and Welfare, (D) Business, (E) Fashion and Home Economics, (F) Culture and General Education (medicine, nursing, piloting etc. not available).
eligibility.return_obligation: None (graduates are expected to keep links with Japan and the embassy)

nationality.note: Any nationality with diplomatic relations with Japan (Japan has none with North Korea). Each Japanese embassy decides whether it recruits for these two categories in a given year and sets its own deadline - check your embassy's notice. Previous MEXT degree grantees and people applying to another MEXT category in the same year are not eligible.

language.note: Japanese is taught in the included 1-year preparatory course; all college classes are in Japanese. Embassy written exams: KOSEN - Japanese, English, Mathematics and Physics or Chemistry; Specialized Training College - Japanese, English and Mathematics.

field.note: KOSEN track is engineering/architecture only; the Specialized Training College track covers technology, nutrition/personal care, education and welfare, business, fashion and home economics, culture. Pick the track that matches your field.

timeline.opening_month: April (embassies recruit April to May for arrival the next April)
timeline.typical_deadline: May to June of the year before arrival, set by each Japanese embassy
timeline.interview_period: First screening (written exams + interview) at the embassy, May to August
timeline.result_announcement: Final results after January (KOSEN) / after February (Specialized Training College) of the arrival year
timeline.course_start: Arrival in Japan 1-7 April; 1-year Japanese preparatory course, then KOSEN 3rd year (3 years; 3.5 for maritime) or a 2-year specialized training college course

deadline.label: Japanese embassy deadline in your country (Embassy Recommendation, KOSEN / Specialized Training College)
deadline.note: MEXT: 'Recruitment for students arriving next April is made between April and May of the previous year; first screening May-August by Japanese Embassies or Consulates General.' Each embassy sets its own date. Embassy notices for the 2027 arrival indexed by search showed e.g. Maldives 17 May 2026, Zimbabwe 29 May 2026, Georgia 5 June 2026 and Singapore 24 June 2026 (Senshu), but those embassy pages block automated access and were not opened, so treat these as unconfirmed examples. The April 2027 cycle is therefore closed; the next one (arrival April 2028) should open about April 2027 - check your embassy from March 2027.

documents.label: FY Application Form (KOSEN or Specialized Training College version) - 1 original + 1 copy
Photograph 4.5 x 3.5 cm, upper body, taken within 6 months (name and nationality on the back), attached to the application form
Academic transcript(s) for all school years of the last school/university attended (upper secondary; plus university if attended), showing the grade scale
documents.notes: Documents must be in Japanese or English, or come with a translation.

documents.label: Certificate of (expected) graduation from upper secondary school
documents.notes: A copy attested by an authorised school official is accepted. KOSEN needs 11 years of schooling; Specialized Training College needs 12 years / upper-secondary completion (by March of the arrival year).

documents.label: University graduation certificate and certificate of enrollment (only if you graduated from / are enrolled at a university)
Recommendation letter from a class teacher or principal of the last school attended (free format; sample available)
Certificate of Health on the FY MEXT form, completed and signed by a physician
Certificate of language proficiency in Japanese or English (only if you have one; issued within the last 2 years; 2 copies)
Embassy written exams (Japanese, English, Mathematics; plus Physics or Chemistry for KOSEN) and interview
Passport (needed for the Student visa before travel)

application_portal_system: Paper application (original + copy) to the Japanese Embassy or Consulate General in your country; do not send documents to MEXT
strategic_tips: Ask your Japanese embassy in March whether it recruits KOSEN and/or Specialized Training College students that year, because windows are short (April-June) and differ by embassy. Practise the written exams (Japanese basics, English, maths; physics or chemistry for KOSEN) since they decide the first screening. The two tracks differ: KOSEN = 4 years in total (1 prep + 3, engineering only, 11 years of schooling needed) and ends with a diploma and the title 'Associate'; Senshu = 3 years (1 prep + 2, broad vocational fields, 12 years of schooling needed) and ends with a diploma.
program_status_note: One record for two MEXT categories with the same nationality, age (born on/after 2 April 2002 for 2027), benefits and embassy process. Differences: schooling (KOSEN 11 years, Senshu 12), duration (KOSEN 4 years incl. prep, 4.5 for maritime; Senshu 3 years), fields and exam subjects (KOSEN adds Physics/Chemistry), result date (KOSEN after Jan, Senshu after Feb). KOSEN graduates may extend to a 2-year advanced course (NIAD-QE bachelor's) or transfer to a national university if MEXT approves.

name: Pan African University (PAU) Scholarships
country: Africa (PAU institutes in Nigeria, Cameroon and Algeria)
organization: African Union Commission - Pan African University Rectorate (Yaounde)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Living-expenses stipend paid by the African Union Commission (amount not published on the official PAU pages)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: PAU states that successful applicants receive 'full scholarships (covering tuition and living expenses)'. Each institute covers students' medical insurance from the disbursed stipend. Travel and accommodation are not described on the official pages - confirm with your institute.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Young, qualified applicants from African countries and the Diaspora
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Master's: undergraduate degree from a recognised university with at least Second Class Upper Division (or equivalent) in a relevant field. PhD: a Master's degree in a relevant field from PAU or any internationally recognised university.
eligibility.language_requirements: No test score stated. Academic competence must be shown in Bachelor's transcripts. Master in Conference Interpreting and Translation: excellent knowledge of at least two African Union official languages (Arabic, English, French, Portuguese, Kiswahili, Spanish).
eligibility.age_limit: 2026-2027 call - Master's: not older than 25 (men) / 28 (women). PhD: maximum 28 (men) / 30 (women). Earlier calls used higher limits (Master's 30/35, PhD 35/40), so check the next call.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Only the programmes of the open PAU institutes: PAULESI (Nigeria: geosciences, reproductive health, plant breeding, environmental management, medicinal plants and drug development, sports management, avian medicine, veterinary vaccines), PAUGHSS (Cameroon: governance and regional integration, conference interpreting, translation, transborder languages) and PAUWES (Algeria: water, energy, climate change - engineering or policy; PhD in the water-energy-climate nexus). PAUSTI (Kenya) did not admit new students in 2026.
eligibility.return_obligation: Scholars commit to serve an African Union Member State after their studies for at least the length of the scholarship.

nationality.note: The call is open to 'applicants from African countries and the Diaspora'. Members of the African diaspora without an African nationality are not covered by this rule - check eligibility with PAU (pau.scholarships@africa-union.org). Special calls have also been run for refugees and displaced people (e.g. Dec 2024 - Jan 2025).

language.note: No IELTS/TOEFL score is set; teaching is in English and/or French depending on the institute (PAUGHSS Cameroon is bilingual). Interpreting/translation applicants need two AU official languages.

field.note: Programme list of the 2026-2027 call; it changes per call (PAUSTI Kenya - science, technology, innovation - paused intake in 2026).

timeline.opening_month: November (2026-2027 call opened 15 Nov 2025); timing has varied between cycles
timeline.typical_deadline: 15 December (2026-2027 call: 15 Nov - 15 Dec 2025). Earlier cycles closed in September (2023, 2020) and a special refugee call closed 22 Jan 2025.
timeline.interview_period: Written/oral examination may follow pre-selection
timeline.course_start: Academic year starts in the second half of the year (exact date set by each institute)

deadline.label: PAU online application (au-pau.org/submission)
deadline.note: The 2026-2027 call ran 15 Nov - 15 Dec 2025 (official PDF, also on au.int). As of 25 Oct 2026 no call for 2027-2028 was published on pau-au.africa. Call dates have moved a lot between cycles (Sept 2023, Sept/Oct 2020, Dec 2025), so this is an estimate. Late applications are not considered.

documents.label: Online application at https://www.au-pau.org/submission/
Certified true copies of relevant university certificates
Certified transcripts (from university and, for Master's, high school)
Certified high-school certificate/transcript (Master's applicants)
Passport or National I.D. card (personal details page; biometric page for PhD)
Clear coloured passport-size photograph (2cm x 2cm)
Detailed CV
Recommendation letter from ONE former university lecturer
documents.notes: Also give the names, emails and WhatsApp numbers of 3 reference university lecturers (mandatory).

documents.label: Recommendation letters from 2 professors
documents.notes: Also give the names, emails and WhatsApp numbers of 3 reference university lecturers (mandatory).

documents.label: 3 to 4-page Research Concept Note (tentative title, research questions, objectives, significance of the research)
Written/oral examination after pre-selection (if required)

application_portal_system: PAU online submission system (au-pau.org/submission)
strategic_tips: PAU calls are short (one month in the last cycle), so prepare certified copies, the recommendation letter and the contacts of 3 referee lecturers before the call opens. Check the age limit for your gender and degree in the new call: the 2026 limits (Master's 25 men / 28 women) were much stricter than earlier ones. Pick a programme that clearly matches your Bachelor's field and mention how you will serve an AU member state afterwards.
program_status_note: 2026-2027 call closed 15 Dec 2025; 2027-2028 call not yet published (checked 25 Oct 2026). PAUSTI (Kenya, at JKUAT) did not admit new students in 2026, so Kenya is not listed as a host; add it back if the next call reopens PAUSTI.

name: AAUW International Fellowships
organization: American Association of University Women (AAUW)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: One-time award paid to the fellow: $20,000 (master's) or $25,000 (doctorate), in two equal payments (start and mid-point of the fellowship year)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: The fellow decides how to spend the stipend on study and living costs. Not allowed: research assistants, publication costs, institutional overhead, dependants' tuition. Not renewable. US tax withholding of 14% or 30% may apply. AAUW gives no visa sponsorship or J-1 waiver help.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Applicants who identify as women and are not U.S. citizens or U.S. permanent residents (green-card applicants are also excluded). When merit is comparable, preference may go to applicants from underrepresented countries, first-time international students, home-country residents, first-generation graduates, single parents and caregivers.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale for the highest degree earned
eligibility.language_requirements: TOEFL iBT 79, TOEFL Essentials 8.5, revised paper-delivered TOEFL 60, IELTS 6.5, Cambridge 176 or Duolingo 120; or a statement that English is your native language, or a diploma/transcript from an English-speaking institution, or one full-time semester at one. Institutional TOEFL is not accepted.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Full-time study in a first master's or an academic/professional doctorate in a STEM program on the U.S. DHS STEM Designated Degree Program list. Eligibility depends on the degree program, not the research topic.

nationality.note: Any non-U.S. citizen who does not hold (or has not applied for) U.S. permanent residency. Fellows normally study in the U.S. Study in a third country (outside both the U.S. and your home country) is allowed only for members of Graduate Women International (GWI) or for citizens of countries under a U.S. travel ban who cannot get a U.S. visa. Applications for 2027-28 closed on 17 Sep 2026.

language.note: IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 79 or Duolingo 120. Native English speakers, or those with a degree (or one full-time semester) from an English-speaking institution, can use that instead. TOEFL, IELTS and Duolingo scores are valid for two years.

field.note: Only programs on the U.S. DHS STEM Designated Degree Program list. Some health, economics and business programs qualify (e.g. biostatistics, econometrics, business analytics) if the program's CIP code is on the DHS list.

timeline.typical_deadline: Mid-September of the year before the fellowship (17 Sep 2026, 5:00 pm ET, for 2027-28)
timeline.course_start: Program must begin on or before 15 Sep 2027 and end on or after 30 Apr 2028

deadline.label: AAUW application portal (5:00 pm ET)
deadline.note: 2027-28 cycle: opened 17 Aug 2026 at 9:00 am ET and closed 17 Sep 2026 at 5:00 pm ET. Already passed; the page now says applications for 2027-28 are closed. Awards announced in March 2027. Dates for the 2028-29 cycle are not yet published; expect a similar Aug-Sep window in 2027. The FAQ mentions a 1 Sep 2027 program start in one place and 15 Sep 2027 in the eligibility section.

documents.label: Online application in the AAUW Fellowships & Grants Application Portal (up to five programs may be listed)
Narrative application (academic/professional plan, commitment to women and girls, career goals and impact, financial plan)
items: Demonstrated academic and/or scholarly excellence
Feasibility of the proposed academic, professional or research plan
Demonstrated commitment to women and girls
Long-term career objectives and commitment to impact
Strength and feasibility of the financial plan
documents.notes: No published word limits. Doctoral applicants are also judged on the originality and potential contribution of the proposed work. Generative AI may assist but not replace your own ideas.

documents.label: 2 letters of recommendation (academic or professional, from professional email addresses; no dossier services)
Copies of all diplomas (or official transcripts showing degree conferral and date); certified English translation for the highest degree
Official transcripts for all degrees, showing a cumulative GPA of at least 3.5/4.0 for the highest degree
Credential evaluation or GPA conversion, if needed to show U.S. bachelor's equivalency or a 3.5/4.0 GPA
Proof of English proficiency (TOEFL iBT 79 / IELTS 6.5 / Duolingo 120 / Cambridge 176)
Admission letter stating the start date (or proof of enrolment for current students)
documents.notes: Enrolling in a program you did not list leads to disqualification. Studying outside both the U.S. and your home country also requires proof of Graduate Women International membership.

application_portal_system: AAUW Fellowships & Grants Application Portal
strategic_tips: Apply only after confirming that your U.S. program's CIP code is on the DHS STEM list and that your highest-degree GPA is at least 3.5/4.0; both are hard cut-offs. Treat the award as one part of your funding: the financial-plan criterion rewards a realistic budget that shows how you will cover the rest of the costs. Show concrete work for women and girls (mentoring, outreach, research focus), because that is a scored criterion.

name: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme (AKF ISP)
country: Global (any reputable university, including local/regional ones; not the UK or Russia)
organization: Aga Khan Foundation (Aga Khan Development Network, AKDN)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Student living expenses, sized to your financial need (no fixed amount published)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Award is 50% grant and 50% loan: you repay half (plus a service charge), starting six months after graduation, ending studies, or losing the award. A guarantor must co-sign. Master's: whole degree; PhD: first two years only. Not covered: international travel, clothing, furniture, family members' living costs.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Outstanding students with no other means of financing from selected countries, for example Afghanistan, Australia, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, the Kyrgyz Republic, Madagascar, Mozambique, New Zealand, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania and Uganda. In countries such as Canada, Portugal and the USA, people originally from one of the listed countries may apply.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Excellent academic record (no numeric minimum published)
eligibility.language_requirements: Set by your admitting university (no programme-wide test)
eligibility.age_limit: No hard limit; preference for young professionals under 30
eligibility.field_restrictions: Any field; full-time postgraduate programmes only (no part-time or short courses). Priority to master's; PhDs considered.

nationality.note: AKDN gives these countries 'for example', so the list may not be complete. In Canada, Portugal, the USA and similar countries, applications are accepted from people originally from a listed country. Applications go through AKF contacts in each country; use the eligibility tool on the official page to check your country and find the local team.

language.note: No AKF test; you need an admission, so meet your university's language requirement.

timeline.opening_month: January (the 2026-27 cycle was open by late January 2026)
timeline.typical_deadline: End of March (the 2025-26 cycle closed 31 March 2025); local offices may set their own dates
timeline.course_start: Autumn of the same year (you must be entering the first year of the programme)

deadline.label: AKF ISP application through your country's AKF office
deadline.note: The official page now says: 'The 2026-2027 application cycle is now closed. The next cycle will open in early 2027.' An archived Dec 2025 copy of the same page said the 2025-2026 cycle closed on 31 March 2025 and the next would open in January 2026. Copies from late Jan and mid-Mar 2026 showed the 2026-27 cycle open; by 22 Apr 2026 it was closed. The exact 2026 and 2027 closing dates are not published. Country offices may close earlier.

documents.label: AKF ISP application form from the AKF contact in your country (via the eligibility tool on the AKDN page)
documents.notes: The full document checklist comes with the country application pack; it is not published online.

documents.label: Admission to a reputable postgraduate institution, for the first year of the programme
documents.notes: Students who have already started their postgraduate studies are not eligible.

documents.label: Academic records showing an excellent academic standing
Bachelor's degree (or equivalent training/professional experience)
Proof of genuine financial need and a multi-source funding plan covering all years of study
Award agreement co-signed by a guarantor (if selected)

application_portal_system: Through the AKF ISP contact/office in your country (eligibility tool on the AKDN website)
strategic_tips: Treat AKF ISP as funding of last resort: show that you have already asked for other scholarships and built a realistic multi-source funding plan, and ask only for the gap. Remember half the award is a loan with a service charge and needs a guarantor, so cost it before you accept. Local and regional universities, and quality distance programmes, are acceptable, but programmes in the UK or Russia are not funded at this time.

name: Bolashak International Scholarship (Bolashaq)
organization: JSC Center for International Programs, Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Monthly stipend for living, food and study materials, set by country under the official expense norms (Order No. 163)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Tuition is paid against a Bolashak financial guarantee letter you send to the university, and the air ticket is bought on request through your curator. Scholars arrange their own visa and medical insurance as the host country requires; whether these are reimbursed is not stated on the public pages. You must provide collateral (a real-estate pledge) or a guarantee under the study agreement.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Citizens of the Republic of Kazakhstan
eligibility.gpa_requirement: General category: no GPA minimum (an unconditional offer from a listed university is the key requirement). Special categories without an offer (rural residents, engineers, medical workers, civil servants, nuclear-sector workers): bachelor's GPA of at least 3.00/4.00 (or 4.00/5.00).
eligibility.language_requirements: Kazakh language certificate (KAZTEST or Qazaq Resmi Test) at level B1 or above for all applicants. Special categories also need a foreign-language certificate meeting the set minimum; the general category meets the university's own requirement through the unconditional offer.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Only specialties on the approved priority list (set from state bodies' requests and labour-market forecasts) at universities on the 2024-2026 list of leading foreign universities. Bachelor's places (20 in 2026) are only for winners/medallists of approved international olympiads or science competitions in the last 3 years.
eligibility.return_obligation: Return within 30 days of finishing and work continuously in Kazakhstan in your specialty: 5 years in Astana, Almaty or Shymkent, 3 years in other regions (one year less if you completed a fully tuition-free admission); 2 years for internships

nationality.note: Kazakhstan citizens only. 2026 allocation: 635 scholarships (20 bachelor's, 400 master's, 50 doctoral, 165 internships).

language.note: Bolashak requires a KAZTEST or Qazaq Resmi Test certificate at B1+ (this is a scholarship rule, not the language of teaching). English or other language proof is handled through your unconditional offer, or by a foreign-language certificate for the special categories.

field.note: Approved list of priority specialties (bolashak.gov.kz/ru/pretendentu/specialnosti) plus a list of related specialties. The 2026 rules added targeted training for the nuclear sector and an AI internship category.

timeline.typical_deadline: Mid-October (16 Oct 2026); selection runs on a rolling basis from mid-April to 31 December
timeline.interview_period: Competitive selection 13 Apr - 31 Dec 2026 (rolling)

deadline.label: Bolashak document submission on egov.kz closes
deadline.note: 2026 round (official): documents accepted 16 Mar-16 Oct 2026 via egov.kz, with competitive selection 13 Apr-31 Dec 2026. Selection is rolling, so for a September 2027 start, apply in spring 2027 as soon as you hold the unconditional offer, not at the October cut-off. The 2027 round dates are not yet announced; expect a similar March-October window. ('Scientific internships' is a separate programme, open until 30 Oct 2026.)

documents.label: Application on egov.kz (Bolashak competition)
Identity card and passport

Unconditional offer (except for financial conditions) from a university on the Bolashak list, stating your details, specialty, study period and tuition cost, with notarised Kazakh or Russian translation
documents.notes: Not required for the special categories (rural residents, engineers, medical workers, civil servants), which apply without an offer but need a GPA of at least 3.0 and work experience.

documents.label: Bachelor's/specialist diploma with supplement (with recognition/nostrification if earned abroad)
State school-leaving (or technical/vocational) certificate with supplement
Diploma (1st-3rd place) from an approved international olympiad or science/performance competition in the last 3 years, matching your chosen specialty
KAZTEST or Qazaq Resmi Test certificate, level B1 or higher
Medical certificate form 072/u for travel abroad
Motivation essay (max 500 words, in Kazakh or Russian, dated and signed): why this university, why you need the scholarship, expected results and how you will apply them
Official record of current grades from your foreign university (only if you are already studying at a listed foreign university), with notarised translation
Proof of employment and pension-contribution statement (special categories: rural, engineering, medical, civil service, nuclear)
Study agreement with the Center and collateral (real-estate pledge) or guarantee, signed after you win

application_portal_system: egov.kz (Bolashak e-service) and the applicant account on konkurs.bolashak.gov.kz
strategic_tips: Secure an unconditional offer from a university on the official 2024-2026 list in a priority specialty first. Without it the general category is closed, and conditional offers do not count. Take the KAZTEST/Qazaq Resmi Test (B1) early and plan your collateral or guarantor before you win, because the agreement cannot be signed without it. Weigh the work obligation (5 years in Astana/Almaty/Shymkent, 3 in the regions) when choosing a specialty.

name: IAEA Marie Sklodowska-Curie Fellowship Programme (MSCFP)
country: Global (any accredited university, including in your own country)
organization: International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Up to EUR 20,000 towards living costs for the whole master's programme (paid only if you hold no other scholarship)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Up to EUR 20,000 for tuition for the whole programme. A limited number of competitive internships (IAEA or partners such as IAEA Collaborating Centres) after the studies. If you hold another scholarship, MSCFP covers tuition only.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Female students from IAEA Member States
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Preference for above-average academic credentials (75% or above, or GPA above 3.0/4.0)
eligibility.language_requirements: All application documents must be in English (or with official English translations); no test score is required by MSCFP
eligibility.field_restrictions: Master's programme in a nuclear-related field relevant to the IAEA's work: nuclear engineering, nuclear physics and chemistry, nuclear medicine, isotopic techniques, radiation biology, nuclear safety, nuclear security, non-proliferation, nuclear law and similar

nationality.note: Open to women from all IAEA Member States (about 180 countries). North Korea (withdrew in 1994) and Taiwan are not Member States; a few small states are also not members, so check the IAEA list of Member States if unsure. Fellows have studied in 76 countries, including their own (for example a Brazilian fellow at the University of Sao Paulo).

language.note: MSCFP asks for no English test; your university's own language requirement applies.

field.note: Nuclear-related master's only. Add a keyword such as 'nuclear' or 'medical physics' to field_keywords in your profile if your program is nuclear-related but your field name does not show it.

timeline.typical_deadline: 31 October (2025 and 2026 cycles); 30 September in 2024
timeline.result_announcement: By e-mail to all applicants (timing not published)

deadline.label: MSCFP online application (you must already be admitted to or enrolled in the master's)
deadline.note: One call per year, in the autumn, for women who are already admitted to or enrolled in a nuclear-related master's. So for a September 2027 start you would normally apply in the autumn 2027 cycle (about 31 Oct 2027), unless you hold your admission letter before 31 Oct 2026. Official dates: 2024 cycle opened 12 Jul and closed 30 Sep 2024; 2025 cycle opened 1 Sep and closed 31 Oct 2025 (IAEA news). The IAEA applicant page says the 2026 cycle is open until 31 Oct 2026; we read that through search results and the European Nuclear Society notice, because iaea.org blocked automated access.

documents.label: Completed MSCFP online application form (in English)
Copy of passport or national ID
Official acceptance/admission letter into the master's programme stating the nuclear-related field and programme duration, plus a statement/confirmation of tuition fees
documents.notes: Translate into English officially if not already in English.

documents.label: Completed MSCFP reference template, sent directly by the referee (1 mandatory, a 2nd is preferred)
documents.notes: Only one reference is mandatory; referees send the form to MSCFP by the application deadline.

documents.label: Documents about any other scholarship you hold for the same master's (if applicable)
documents.notes: Declaring another scholarship reduces MSCFP support to tuition only.

application_portal_system: MSCFP online application form (linked from the IAEA 'Information for applicants' page)
strategic_tips: Secure your admission letter first: MSCFP only funds women already accepted or enrolled, so time your application for the autumn call after you are admitted. Make the nuclear link explicit in your admission letter and motivation (programme title, thesis topic), and explain how the degree serves public service or your country's nuclear programme, since the committee also weighs field, geographic and linguistic diversity. Line up two referees early; one reference is mandatory and the second is preferred.

name: Japan-IMF Scholarship Program for Asia (JISPA)
organization: International Monetary Fund Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific (OAP), funded by the Government of Japan

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Monthly stipend covering living expenses and health insurance premiums (amount not published)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Full university tuition and one round-trip airfare. Master's Track: a 2.5-month Orientation Program in Japan (academic English, mathematics, introductory economics/econometrics, introductory Japanese) and an English-test allowance if you registered the JISPA code on your TOEFL/IELTS. Ph.D. Track: admission and tuition fees, stipend, airfare and possible support for field research and conferences; insurance is paid from the stipend; no family costs.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Nationals of Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyz Republic, Lao P.D.R., Malaysia, Maldives, Mongolia, Nepal, Pacific Island Countries, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Vietnam
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No numeric minimum; transcripts, a grading-system explanation and a math test (all eligible Master's applicants) are assessed
eligibility.language_requirements: TOEFL iBT 79-80 or IELTS 6.0 overall. Exempt: nationals of India, the Philippines and selected Pacific Island Countries, and graduates of English-medium programs in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the UK or the US. Applicants without a score may take a JISPA in-house test.
eligibility.age_limit: No hard limit; priority to applicants under 36 (Master's) or under 38 (Ph.D.)
eligibility.field_restrictions: Economics and public policy (Master's Track at GRIPS, Hitotsubashi, International University of Japan or the University of Tokyo); economics or related fields at any accredited Japanese university (Ph.D. Track). Applicants must be officials currently employed and nominated by a central bank, ministry of finance/economy/planning/trade, tax administration, statistics bureau, financial regulator or similar macroeconomic agency.
eligibility.return_obligation: Must return to the nominating agency after the studies (the agency guarantees reinstatement)

nationality.note: From the AY2027-28 Master's Track guidelines. The guidelines say 'Pacific Island Countries' without naming them; the Pacific entries here (Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, Palau, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu) are our expansion to the Pacific island IMF members, so confirm with jispa@imf.org. You must also be a government official at a key economic agency and be nominated by it. Officials on leave or off duty for more than one consecutive month in the 12 months before 1 Jul 2027 are not eligible.

language.note: TOEFL iBT 79-80 or IELTS 6.0 (test taken after 1 Dec 2024). English-medium degrees count only if earned in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the UK or the US; nationals of India, the Philippines and selected Pacific Island Countries are exempt. Without a score you may sit a JISPA in-house English test.

field.note: Master's Track programs are in economics or public policy; Ph.D. Track in economics or related fields.

timeline.typical_deadline: Master's Track: 20 October of the year before (23:59 JST), references by 1 November. Ph.D. Track: 1 June of the intake year.
timeline.interview_period: Math test 3 Dec 2026; interviews late January to mid-February 2027
timeline.course_start: Orientation in Japan from 9 July 2027; master's programs begin mid-September to 1 October 2027

deadline.label: Master's Track online application (23:59 JST)

extra.label: Reference letters due (Master's Track)
Ph.D. Track application (23:59 JST); secure your Japanese university admission yourself

deadline.note: AY2027-28 Master's Track: online window 15 Sep-20 Oct 2026 (23:59 JST), already closed; two reference letters must reach jispa@imf.org by 1 Nov 2026. Ph.D. Track: window 1 May-1 Jun 2027 (23:59 JST) for September/October 2027 or April 2028 admission, with guidelines posted by early March 2027. The IMF says the dates are indicative and may change.

documents.label: JISPA online application (see the sample application form)
Agency Nomination and Certification Form, signed by the authorised official with the agency's seal (confirms support and reinstatement after study)
Research proposal for a thesis or policy paper on a policy issue in your country (max 500 words, Word file)
Statement of purpose: goals, choice of partner universities and field, fit, and how JISPA helps your agency and country (400-600 words, Word file)
Official transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate schools, plus the grading system and GPA explanation (or a completed GPA calculator)
Certified copies of diplomas/degree certificates (sealed by the university's administration office)
TOEFL iBT 79-80 or IELTS 6.0 certificate (test taken after 1 Dec 2024), if available
documents.notes: Applicants without a score are asked to take a JISPA in-house test before a final decision; some applicants are exempt.

documents.label: Copy of passport photo page (or national ID with photo)
Recent passport-style photo (JPG, max 500 KB)
2 reference letters from supervisors, academic advisors or professional referees, sent by the referees from official institutional email to jispa@imf.org
JISPA math test (3 Dec 2026 for AY2027-28) and interview
Admission to a doctoral program at an accredited Japanese university (Ph.D. Track; you apply to the university yourself)

application_portal_system: JISPA Online Application System (linked from the IMF JISPA application page)
strategic_tips: This is only for officials of central banks, finance/economy/planning ministries, tax and statistics offices and similar agencies, so secure your agency's signed nomination early; it is mandatory. Keep the research proposal focused on a concrete macro or fiscal policy problem in your country (500 words max) and practise for the December math test. Ask referees in advance: they must email their letters from official institutional addresses after you submit and get your reference number.

name: Mexican Government Excellence Scholarships for Foreigners (Becas de Excelencia del Gobierno de México para Extranjeros)
organization: Mexican Agency for International Development Cooperation (AMEXCID), Ministry of Foreign Affairs (SRE)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Master's: 4 x the monthly UMA (MXN 14,264.88 in the 2026 call); doctoral and postdoctoral research stays: 5 x UMA (MXN 17,831.10). Paid monthly in arrears.
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Enrolment and tuition per the host institution's acceptance letter; IMSS health insurance from the 7th month of the scholarship (buy your own international insurance for the first months); Mexican visa fee waiver; economy return airfare home at the end, for nationals of countries listed in Annex 3; domestic transport between Mexico City and the host city if outside Mexico City (Annex 4). Bring funds for at least the first 60 days.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Citizens of the countries and territories listed in Annex 5 (more than 170 countries) of the call (Latin America, Caribbean, Africa, Asia, Europe, Middle East, Pacific). Not eligible: Mexican nationals (including children of Mexican parents), people living in Mexico without a student residence card, foreign diplomats in Mexico and their families, current Mexican-government scholarship holders, and people living outside their country of nationality.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Minimum 85/100 (8.5/10) in the Mexican-equivalent grading scale, stated in the acceptance letter and shown on the latest transcript
eligibility.language_requirements: Spanish B2 (CEFR) certificate if your native language is not Spanish. If the program is taught in another language, the host must provide a letter committing to tutoring in that language.
eligibility.age_limit: 18 or older at the time of application
eligibility.field_restrictions: Any full-time, in-person program at the 90 eligible Mexican institutions (Annex 1, mostly programs in Mexico's national postgraduate system). No funding for thesis-writing only. Research stays give preference to food systems, gender equality, water, renewable energy, inequality, sustainable consumption, climate change and terrestrial ecosystems.

countries: Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha
nationality.note: From Annex 5 (eligible countries) of the 2026 call. 'Western Sahara' and the 'Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic' both appear and are merged as Sahrawi Republic. Not listed (so not eligible in 2026): United States, Ecuador, Afghanistan, Myanmar, Yemen and others. You must live in your country of nationality and must not be nominated or sponsored by institutions outside it. The 2027 call (and its annexes) is not yet published; the list can change.

language.note: Spanish B2 certificate needed at application unless Spanish is your native language. Applications must be written in Spanish.

field.note: Any program at an eligible Mexican institution (Annex 1). For research stays, preference goes to sustainability, food, water, energy, climate, gender equality and inequality topics.

timeline.opening_month: May (21 May 2026 for the 2026 call); the month varies by year
timeline.typical_deadline: About one month after the call opens (22 Jun 2026, 3:00 pm Central Mexico time, in 2026)

The call comes out each year, but the timing moves (aggregators report the previous call closed in September 2025, unverified). The 2027 call is not yet published, so watch gob.mx/amexcid from about May 2027. Your host acceptance letter must be issued no more than 60 days before you apply.

Submit early in the window, because the call says earlier applications get preference and places are shared by country. The PhD and postdoc options are 6-12 month research stays, not full doctoral degrees. Only the master's covers a whole degree (up to 24 months).

coverage_details.additional_allowances: Travel to and from the host institute, visa expenses, a yearly medical insurance contribution, a modest annual research support allowance, and invitations to regional science-communication and proposal-writing workshops. Study fees (tuition, registration) are covered jointly by OWSD and the host institute. Figures are from the 2022 programme leaflet.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Women scientists from Science and Technology Lagging Countries (STLCs) listed by OWSD (Africa, Arab region, Asia-Pacific and Latin America & Caribbean).
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Not published while the programme is suspended

eligibility.field_restrictions: PhD research in STEM fields
eligibility.return_obligation: Fellows are expected to contribute to the development of their home countries; no formal bond is published

nationality.note: Eligible-country list from the official OWSD PhD Fellowship leaflet (2022), the latest list the site still links. SUSPENDED: OWSD says there was no PhD call in 2025 because of funding, and no new call had been announced by Oct 2026. The list may change if the programme returns.

language.note: No programme-wide test was published; the host institute's language rules apply.

Watch owsd.net/phd-fellowships for a new call and look at the OWSD Early Career Fellowship, which is still listed, if you already hold a PhD. When it ran, there were two options: a full-time PhD of up to 4 years at a host institute in another developing country, or a 'sandwich' PhD registered at your home institute with visits of at least 6 months at a time to a host abroad.
program_status_note: Suspended: OWSD announced no PhD call in 2025 for funding reasons, and none had been announced by 25 Oct 2026.

name: Russian Government Scholarship (Quota of the Government of the Russian Federation)
organization: Government of the Russian Federation, run by Rossotrudnichestvo (Russian Houses) and Russian embassies/consulates with the Ministry of Science and Higher Education

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: State academic scholarship paid monthly for the whole period of study (amount set by each university under Russian rules; small)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Free tuition for the whole programme, including a preparatory year of Russian if you need it. A dormitory place is usually offered but you pay a subsidised fee (the portal cites about RUB 300-20,000/month; NUST MISIS charges quota students RUB 2,500-3,769/month). You must buy voluntary medical insurance (DMS, about RUB 4,000-20,000/year) and pay your own travel.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Foreign citizens of countries that receive quota places (places are allocated per country). Russian citizens are excluded, except dual nationals who live permanently abroad and hold no Russian education documents.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No fixed minimum; ranked on documents (portfolio, achievements) and, in some countries, on interviews or tests
eligibility.language_requirements: Not required at application: most programmes are taught in Russian and the quota includes a preparatory Russian year. Some universities offer English-taught programmes.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Any field offered by participating state universities (you list up to 6 universities in priority order: at most 2 in Moscow, 2 in St Petersburg and 3 in one federal district)

nationality.note: Any foreign citizen may register, but places are allocated per country each year and the first selection stage is run in your country by Rossotrudnichestvo (Russian House) or the Russian embassy/consulate. Ask them how many places your country has. Media reported in Oct 2026 that Rossotrudnichestvo plans to change how quota places are shared between countries from 2027; no official rules were published by 25 Oct 2026.

language.note: No language certificate at application. Teaching is mostly in Russian; if you do not speak Russian, ask for the preparatory year in your application.

timeline.typical_deadline: 15 January for most countries (CIS countries may close earlier; some countries get extensions)
timeline.interview_period: First stage (interviews/tests in your country) roughly Feb-April
timeline.result_announcement: First-stage results usually April-May; university placement in summer
timeline.course_start: September (after the preparatory year if you need Russian)

deadline.label: Quota application on education-in-russia.com (most countries)

extra.label: CIS countries (per NUST MISIS for 2027/28; not yet confirmed on the national portal)

deadline.note: Official portal news: the 2026/27 campaign opened 15 Sep 2025 and closed for most candidates on 15 Jan 2026, with later extensions for a few countries (e.g. Bosnia, Serbia, North Macedonia 31 Jan; Iran 13 Feb; Georgia 15 Feb; Laos 20 Mar; Vietnam 31 Mar; Botswana 15 Mar 2026). The 2025/26 campaign also closed 15 Jan 2025. For 2027/28 the portal had not posted dates by 25 Oct 2026; NUST MISIS (a participating state university) lists 15 Dec 2026 for CIS countries and 15 Jan 2027 for all others. Your local Russian House/embassy may set its own deadline, so confirm with them.

Scan of passport (or other identity document)
Photograph

Scan of grades (transcript / diploma supplement)

Proof of achievements (diplomas, certificates, awards, list of publications)
Interview and/or selection tests with Rossotrudnichestvo or the embassy (depends on your country)
Medical certificate (no HIV infection and no contraindications to study), in Russian or with notarised translation
Education documents with notarised Russian translation, legalised or apostilled where required

application_portal_system: Education in Russia for Foreigners portal (GIS ORFI, education-in-russia.com)
strategic_tips: Register early on education-in-russia.com and contact your local Russian House or embassy: they run the first stage, can set an earlier local deadline, and decide how your country's quota is shared. Upload achievements (olympiads, certificates, publications) because the first stage ranks candidates within each country. List six universities spread across regions, since only two Moscow and two St Petersburg choices are allowed. Budget for insurance, dormitory fees and flights, which the quota does not pay.

name: Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques Scholarship Program (برنامج خادم الحرمين الشريفين للابتعاث)
organization: Ministry of Education, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Monthly allowance paid through the Saudi cultural mission in the host country (amount by country; not published on the MoE or Qabul pages)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Government sponsorship of tuition and study costs at the approved institution. The MoE page says eligible family companions can be added to the scholarship decision and travel tickets. Health insurance and other allowances are not described on the official pages we could read (Saudi cultural missions are widely reported to provide insurance), so they are left unconfirmed.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Saudi nationals only
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Depends on the track: some tracks rank by university ranking and academic average without a fixed minimum; health tracks set minimums (e.g. master's in nursing/applied medical sciences: bachelor's GPA of at least 2.75/4, 3.75/5 or 80%)
eligibility.language_requirements: Depends on the track and the admitting university (e.g. health tracks: IELTS 5.5 or TOEFL iBT 46).
eligibility.age_limit: Track-specific (e.g. health tracks: up to 25 for bachelor's, up to 30 for master's); other tracks have no published age limit
eligibility.field_restrictions: Only approved institutions and specializations for each track: Pioneers (Al-Rowad, top 30 institutions worldwide), Research & Development, Emdad (top 200 universities, labour-market specialties, including training programs) and Wa'ed (promising sectors), plus the health-agreements track

nationality.note: Saudi nationals of good conduct with direct, unconditional admission to an approved institution and specialization, studying full-time in the country of the institution's main campus, and foreign qualifications need equivalency (general conditions on the MoE scholarship page, written for the 2021-23 tracks; track rules also exclude applicants who already hold a degree at the same level). Your national ID and passport must be valid to submit on Qabul. Up to 3 scholarship applications per student.

language.note: No single program-wide test; your unconditional admission covers the university's language requirement. Some tracks set their own minimums (health tracks: IELTS 5.5).

field.note: Each track publishes approved institution and specialization lists on Qabul (uap.sa); Emdad (listed on Qabul under external scholarship training) targets labour-market needs.

timeline.opening_month: January (main window on Qabul); the Pioneers track opens separately (open until 15 Nov 2026)
timeline.typical_deadline: Early-to-mid May (7 May 2026, extended to 14 May 2026, for international universities)
timeline.result_announcement: Mid-June (12-14 Jun 2026: external scholarship results and confirmation of choice)

deadline.label: Qabul: international universities scholarship applications

extra.label: Pioneers track (top-30 institutions) closes on Qabul

deadline.note: Applications now go through the Ministry of Education's National Unified Admission Platform 'Qabul' (uap.sa). In 2026 the scholarship window ran from January to 7 May, with results and confirmation on 12-14 Jun 2026 (Saudi press: Okaz gives 10 Jan to 7 May from the platform schedule; Sayidaty gives a 29 Jan opening). The Qabul site itself announces the extension of international-university applications to 14 May. As of 25 Oct 2026 the Qabul site shows the Pioneers track (top-30 institutions) open until 15 Nov; which intake that window serves is not stated. The 2027 dates are not yet published; expect a similar Jan-May window.

Valid Saudi national ID (an expired ID blocks the application)

Documents for accompanying family members (to add them to the scholarship decision and tickets)

strategic_tips: Get an unconditional admission at an institution on your track's approved list first; the higher its ranking, the stronger your file (the Pioneers track only covers the world's top 30). Check that your national ID and passport are valid and your Absher data is up to date before the January window opens. You can file up to three scholarship requests, so pair a Pioneers or top-200 option with a safer approved choice.

name: ASRT Master's and PhD Grants – 'Step by Step' / GROWTH (منح الماجستير والدكتوراه – أكاديمية البحث العلمي والتكنولوجيا)
organization: Academy of Scientific Research and Technology (ASRT), Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: None – the grant does not include salaries or monthly incentives (لا تشمل المنحة مرتبات أو حوافز شهرية)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Research grant for the thesis: up to EGP 250,000 for a Master's over 3 years and up to EGP 350,000 for a PhD over 4 years (2026 call, GROWTH programme 'Step by Step – Cycle 2'). It is not a job or a promise of employment.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Egyptian nationals only
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Master's: bachelor's degree graded at least 'Very Good' (جيد جدًا, about 3.0 on a 4.0 scale) from a recognised university. PhD: a master's degree plus at least 'Very Good' in the bachelor's. Applicants are ranked by cumulative grade; practical experience breaks ties, and the h-index of the applicant and main supervisor is considered for PhD.
eligibility.language_requirements: No language test listed.
eligibility.age_limit: Master's: not older than 30; PhD: not older than 35
eligibility.field_restrictions: Priority fields include artificial intelligence, semiconductors, biotechnology, cybersecurity and quantum computing, among others.

nationality.note: Applicants must already be registered in a Master's or PhD programme at an Egyptian university and have finished the preliminary (coursework) year, be affiliated with a research body or an R&D unit of a company or factory, hold no other grant, and have completed or been exempted from military/public service. PhD priority goes to former 'Scientists for Next Generation' (علماء الجيل القادم) grantees.
