timeline.course_start: Grant runs alongside an Egyptian Master's (3 years) or PhD (4 years) that has already started

name: AUC Graduate Fellowships for Egyptians – Egyptian Graduate Fellowship and other institutional fellowships (زمالات الدراسات العليا بالجامعة الأمريكية بالقاهرة)
organization: The American University in Cairo (AUC) – Office of Graduate Studies

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Egyptian Graduate Fellowship: a monthly stipend (amount not published), in return for 18 hours a week of teaching assistantship
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Egyptian Graduate Fellowship (full institutional fellowship, Master's): tuition for up to 9 credits per semester, monthly stipend, student services and activities fees, medical service and health insurance fees, and possibly remedial English modules (not the intensive ELI course); up to five semesters plus one summer (seven semesters for Counseling Psychology). Other fellowships (University Fellowships, Laboratory Instruction Graduate Fellowships for science and engineering, Writing Center fellowships, named endowed fellowships, Allehedan fellowship for Arab PhD/MSc students) give full tuition for 9 credits or partial tuition for 1–8 credits, usually renewed semester by semester.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Egyptian Graduate Fellowship: Egyptian nationals only. University Fellowships and Laboratory Instruction Fellowships: all nationalities. Mohammed Bin Abdulkarim A. Allehedan Fellowship: nationals of Arab countries admitted to PhD or MSc science and engineering programmes.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Egyptian Graduate Fellowship: bachelor's degree with an overall GPA of at least 3.2/4.0 (or equivalent) and AUC graduate admission; keep a 3.2 GPA. Continuing students need a 3.2 GPA to apply for or keep most fellowships. Selection weighs academic merit and financial need.
eligibility.language_requirements: Full graduate admission: TOEFL iBT 79 (writing 21) or IELTS Academic 6.5 (writing 7); some programmes require more. Applicants provisionally admitted with remedial English are still eligible for fellowships.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Any AUC graduate degree programme. Not eligible for institutional fellowships: graduate diplomas, Master of Engineering (M Eng), Master in Computing (M Comp) and non-degree study. No fellowships for the Architecture MSc.

nationality.note: This record targets Egyptians (Egyptian Graduate Fellowship). Egyptians can also compete for all-nationality fellowships (University Fellowships, Laboratory Instruction Fellowships) and, for PhD/MSc in science and engineering, the Allehedan Fellowship for Arab nationals. AUC staff and dependents using tuition remission cannot combine it with fellowships.

language.note: IELTS 6.5 overall with 7.0 in writing, or TOEFL iBT 79 with 21 in writing, for full admission. Lower scores can lead to provisional admission with remedial English, which still allows a fellowship.

timeline.typical_deadline: Fall 2027: cycle 1 22 Dec 2026 – 17 Jan 2027; cycle 2 6 Apr – 6 May 2027. Admission application at least two weeks before the fellowship deadline (degree admission deadlines: 15 Dec 2026 early, 1 Apr 2027 regular).

extra.label: Graduate admission application, early deadline

Graduate admission deadlines for Fall 2027: 15 Dec 2026 (early) and 1 Apr 2027 (regular). Spring 2027 fellowships: 7 Oct – 2 Nov 2026.

The Egyptian Graduate Fellowship needs a 3.2 GPA and comes with 18 hours a week of teaching-assistant work, so mention any teaching or lab experience in your statement of purpose. Aim for IELTS 6.5 with 7 in writing (or TOEFL 79 with 21 in writing) to avoid remedial English and finish within the five funded semesters.
program_status_note: Al Alfi PhD Fellowship in Applied Sciences and Engineering and Al Alfi Biotechnology Fellowship (both for Egyptians) show 'No new intake'. Egyptian men must also show their military status certificate at admission.

name: AUC Undergraduate Scholarships for Egyptians – Public-School Scholarship Fund (PSSF) and Excellence Scholarships (منح الجامعة الأمريكية بالقاهرة)
organization: The American University in Cairo (AUC)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: None for PSSF and Excellence awards; some donor-funded scholarships add a stipend or book allowance
coverage_details.additional_allowances: PSSF (Egyptian public-school graduates with financial need): tuition and fees, a double room in the AUC dorms for students living outside Cairo and Giza, and AUC transportation for students not in the dorms. Excellence Scholarships (merit, sensitive to need): academic achievement 20%–100% of tuition, plus talents, leadership and community service, and liberal-arts-major awards up to 30% each; awards can be combined up to 100%. Donor-funded scholarships may include housing, transport, stipends and books.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: PSSF: Egyptian students who graduate from public, experimental, STEM and Nile schools in the current year. Excellence Scholarships: all certificates (national, international, private and public schools); international students compete in a separate category.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: PSSF: an outstanding secondary-school record and demonstrated financial need, plus AUC admission requirements. Excellence: academic scores are the main criterion and scholarship cut-offs are 'significantly higher than admission' and change every semester; students compete against peers with the same certificate. No fixed percentage is published.
eligibility.language_requirements: PSSF: IELTS Academic 5.5 (writing 5.5), TOEFL iBT 62 (writing 17) or Duolingo 115–120, taken within two years of the term start. All undergraduates must submit TOEFL, IELTS Academic or Duolingo for English placement; lower scores mean English Language Institute courses before regular study.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Any AUC undergraduate major (science and engineering majors are declared on admission; places are limited). The Liberal Arts Majors award is limited to anthropology, Arabic studies, Egyptology, English and comparative literature, film, history, Middle East studies, music, philosophy, sociology, theatre and visual arts.

nationality.note: PSSF is for Egyptians from public, experimental, STEM and Nile schools only. Excellence Scholarships are also open to other nationalities, but this record covers Egyptian applicants. PSSF is offered for the Fall semester only.

language.note: PSSF minimum: IELTS 5.5 with writing 5.5, TOEFL iBT 62 with writing 17, or Duolingo 115–120. AUC does not exempt anyone because of citizenship or an English-medium school.

timeline.opening_month: Late October (scholarship and financial-assessment applications for Aid Year 2027-2028 open on Banner in late October)
timeline.typical_deadline: Fall 2027: early admission 1 February 2027, regular admission 1 June 2027 (priority for higher-percentage awards goes to complete files by 1 February)
timeline.result_announcement: Provisional/early admission decisions after the February round; final admission after Thanaweya Amma results

Public, experimental, STEM and Nile school students with financial need should aim for PSSF, which also gives a dorm room to students from outside Cairo and Giza. Take IELTS or TOEFL in grade 12 (PSSF needs at least IELTS 5.5) and ask two teachers for recommendation letters early.

name: Digital Egypt Pioneers Initiative – DEPI (مبادرة رواد مصر الرقمية)
organization: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT), Egypt

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: None
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Free training scholarship (منحة رواد مصر الرقمية المجانية) with technology partners, aimed at freelancing on global platforms or specialised jobs. 2026 (round 5) tracks – DEPI: data analysis, AI and data science, software development, ERP, digital marketing and digital arts, game design and development, infrastructure and cybersecurity; DEPI Industry (limited seats): AI tracks for teachers, medical services, legal specialists, marketing automation, AI-assisted software development, and a consultant track. Training includes partner certifications.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Egyptian youth: university students and graduates of all faculties (during or after university)
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No grade requirement published; selection is through the initiative's admission process and tests.
eligibility.language_requirements: No formal certificate required; an English level check may be part of selection (reported by non-official guides, not confirmed).
eligibility.field_restrictions: Open to students and graduates of all faculties; the training itself is in digital and IT fields.

nationality.note: MCIT's 2024 notice (relayed by Assiut University) describes a free scholarship for Egyptian students and graduates of all colleges. Residence in Egypt and an English test are mentioned only by unofficial guides.

language.note: Training partners use English material; no test certificate is required to register.

field.note: Anyone can join regardless of degree; the tracks are digital/IT skills.

timeline.typical_deadline: Registration stays open for a limited window (one month in 2024); DEPI Industry closes as soon as seats are filled
timeline.interview_period: Admission/placement tests after registration (reported by applicant guides)

deadline.note: Round 5 (2026) registration opened 8 June 2026 according to Egypt Telegraph (10 Jun 2026), which cites the MCIT website; no closing date was published, and DEPI Industry closes when seats are full. MCIT's 2024 notice said registration would open in the first week of July 2024 for one month only. The day used here is only a planning estimate (about one month after opening); register as soon as the round opens on depi.gov.eg.

application_portal_system: depi.gov.eg online registration (contact: info@depi.gov.eg)
strategic_tips: DEPI is free and runs from Egypt, so it suits students and graduates who want job-ready IT skills without travelling; register on the first days of a new round because some tracks close when seats fill. Pick one track that matches your goal (data analysis and digital marketing are open to non-IT graduates) and practise basic English and problem-solving before the admission tests. Follow depi.gov.eg and the official DEPI Facebook page for the round announcement (June in 2026).
program_status_note: Launched by MCIT in late 2023; round 5 opened in June 2026. Not to be confused with the separate presidential 'Digital Pioneers' (الرواد الرقميون / Digilians) residential programme at the Egyptian Military Academy, or with the self-paced partner courses now promoted on depi.gov.eg.

name: Digital Pioneers Presidential Initiative – Digilians (مبادرة الرواد الرقميون)
organization: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) with the Egyptian Military Academy

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: None stated
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Described as a free training grant when launched (EgyptInnovate, Apr 2025; the 2026 announcement mentions no fees), with full board and accommodation at Egyptian Military Academy facilities (military complex in the New Administrative Capital and the Military Academy in Heliopolis). Programmes: intensive diploma (4 months, 590+ training hours, with industry partners), specialised diploma (9 months, 1,300+ hours, with the National Telecommunication Institute and the Military Technical College, blended face-to-face and e-learning) and professional master's (12 months, 1,700+ hours, with Queen's University in Canada and a Malaysian partner university). Includes English, soft skills, practical training with 30+ global companies and physical fitness programmes; certificates from MCIT and the Military Academy plus international certifications.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Egyptian young people aged 18 to 32 from all governorates and all academic and professional backgrounds
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No grade requirement published; admission procedures select the best candidates.
eligibility.language_requirements: No test certificate required; English training is part of the programme.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Training in artificial intelligence, programming, cybersecurity, data science and digital arts.

nationality.note: Presidential initiative for Egyptian youth (launched 2025). Residential programme on Military Academy premises.

timeline.typical_deadline: Mid-May (second cohort 2026: registration open until mid-May)
timeline.interview_period: Admission procedures after registration (details not published)

deadline.label: Registration on digilians.gov.eg (closes mid-May)
deadline.note: MCIT announced the second cohort on 21 April 2026 with registration until 'mid-May' (Masrawy, Al-Watan and Assiut University relayed the ministry statement); no exact closing day was published. The first cohort was launched in April 2025 (EgyptInnovate, 27 Apr 2025). A third cohort for 2027 has not been announced.

Egyptian national ID (age 18–32)

strategic_tips: This is a free, residential IT programme inside Egypt: training, food and housing are on Military Academy premises, so families should read the residence and discipline rules before applying. Choose the 4-month intensive diploma if you want a fast job-ready path, or the 12-month professional master's if you already have a degree. Registration opens in spring and closed in mid-May in 2026, so watch MCIT announcements from April 2027.
program_status_note: Different from DEPI (مبادرة رواد مصر الرقمية, depi.gov.eg). In April 2025 EgyptInnovate also listed a 24-month Master of Science track; the 2026 call lists only the three programmes above.

name: Egyptian Government Missions Abroad – external PhD, joint supervision and scientific missions (البعثات الخارجية والإشراف المشترك – وزارة التعليم العالي)
organization: Central Administration for Missions, Cultural Affairs and Missions Sector (قطاع الشئون الثقافية والبعثات), Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Mission allowance set by the Egyptian missions regulations (varies by country and mission type; not published in the calls)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Missions are funded by the state ('على نفقة البعثات'); the detailed allowances (monthly allowance, travel, insurance) follow the missions regulations and are not stated in the public calls, so confirm them with your university's missions office. Mission types in the last unified call: full PhD abroad (3–4 years), joint supervision (one year of research abroad during an Egyptian PhD), scientific missions/postdoc (up to 6 months), Master's abroad (1 year, renewable once), and a Japan-only year to collect Master's data (EJEP). Egyptian–French joint PhD scholarships (2025/26 call): 6-month PhD research stays, or 12- or 18-month joint-supervision stays split into 6-month periods; about 100 joint PhD scholarships planned over five years.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Egyptian staff of public universities, institutes and research centres listed in the missions plan (faculty members, demonstrators/assistant lecturers – معيدون ومدرسون مساعدون – and researchers); not open to the general public
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Depends on the mission type: bachelor's degree for most types, a master's or a registered PhD topic for others. PhD and joint-supervision applicants must be recently registered (generally within 18 months for PhD; within one year for Master's registration), per the last unified call (2022).
eligibility.language_requirements: IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 79 for most mission types in the last unified call (exemptions in some cases, e.g. degrees earned in the same-language country); JLPT N3 for Japanese-language missions. The host university's higher level must also be met.
eligibility.age_limit: Last unified call (2022), at the start of the announcement: about 33 for a full PhD mission, 35 for joint supervision, 30 for Master's-related missions, 40–55 for scientific missions depending on academic rank. The 2026–2031 plan's limits are not yet published.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Missions follow national priority axes: energy, water, medical sciences and health, agriculture and food security, environment, strategic industrial technologies, ICT/space/communications, education, investment/trade/transport, and social sciences/humanities/arts. The 2026–2031 strategic plan highlights artificial intelligence, water desalination and renewable energy.
eligibility.return_obligation: Not stated in the calls reviewed. Mission members are sent by their Egyptian university or research centre and return to their posts; confirm the service period required after the mission with your institution.

nationality.note: Only for Egyptians employed at Egyptian public universities, institutes or research centres included in the missions plan (assistant lecturers, lecturers, faculty, researchers), nominated through their institution. Fresh graduates who are not appointed as demonstrators cannot apply.

language.note: Level from the last unified call (2022): IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 79; check the new call.

timeline.opening_month: Varies (the last unified call opened 12 February 2022; new calls under the 2026–2031 plan not yet announced)
timeline.typical_deadline: Varies by call (last unified call closed 11 April 2022; Egyptian–French joint PhD scholarships had an information session on 26 February 2026)
timeline.interview_period: Scientific committees review research plans and interview applicants (about two months after the call closes in 2022)
timeline.result_announcement: About 2.5 months after the deadline in the 2022 call
timeline.course_start: Within one year of final approval of the results

documents.label: Official data form for the mission type (Arabic, stamped by the sending university), submitted online at eservices.cdm.edu.eg
First university degree certificate with graduation grade, in English (and master's certificate if applicable)
Original language certificate at the required level (IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 79 in the last call)
Sworn statement that you have not received a mission or sponsored scholarship for the same purpose before
Research plan without personal data, stamped (max 3 pages for PhD/Master's, 2 pages for scientific missions)
Acceptance letter or the foreign supervisor's approval
Endorsement letter from the employer (university / research centre)
Names and emails of three academic referees
Medical fitness check before travel

application_portal_system: Missions e-services portal (eservices.cdm.edu.eg) – electronic submission only
strategic_tips: This route is for people already appointed at an Egyptian public university or research centre (معيد / مدرس مساعد / باحث); if that is you, register your Master's or PhD early, because recent registration is a condition, and line up a foreign supervisor's acceptance and IELTS 6.5 before the call opens. Follow the Cultural Affairs and Missions Sector site and your university's missions office for the first calls of the 2026–2031 plan and for bilateral calls such as the Egyptian–French joint PhD scholarships. Ask your institution how long you must serve after returning before you accept a mission.
program_status_note: The last unified missions-plan call found on the official site is for 2021/2022 (applications 12 Feb – 11 Apr 2022, run with JICA under the Egyptian–Japanese Education Partnership). In December 2025 the ministry's Executive Committee for Missions approved a new 2026–2031 strategic plan (ninth five-year plan: master's, joint master's, PhD, skills and training programmes in AI, desalination and renewable energy), and a joint Egyptian–French PhD programme (about 100 joint-supervision PhD scholarships over five years; first cohort 2025/26) is running. No 2027 call or deadline has been published yet. Sources: cdm.mohesr.gov.eg (2025 newsletter, French joint scholarships notice of 23 Feb 2026), Masrawy (4 Dec 2025).

name: Future Scholars Grant (منحة علماء المستقبل) – Ministry of Higher Education scholarship for top students at national (ahliya) universities
organization: Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (MoHESR) with the Central Bank of Egypt – National Initiative to Support Outstanding Students (المبادرة الوطنية لدعم الطلاب المتميزين)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Living costs (الإعاشة) are covered until graduation and paid into the student's own bank account in Egypt; the amount is not published
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Full tuition, accommodation and living costs at one of the 32 participating ahliya universities until graduation, plus extra soft-skills and language programmes. Funding continues only while the student keeps a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 (or equivalent) from the second year, good conduct, and no other parallel grant; the grant is cancelled and must be repaid if these rules are broken (as reported by Masrawy, 1 Mar 2026).

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Egyptian nationals only (أن يحمل الطالب الجنسية المصرية) who graduated from a government (public) secondary school and benefit from Takaful and Karama (تكافل وكرامة) or had their school fees waived by the Ministry of Education
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Academically outstanding Thanaweya Amma (or STEM) graduates of the current year who reach the minimum score announced by the initiative for each faculty (cut-offs are not published in advance). Applicants are ranked electronically by total Thanaweya Amma score within their governorate (or the nearest governorate offering the faculty), then must pass an admission test. At university the student must keep a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 from the second year.
eligibility.language_requirements: No language test is listed for the grant itself. Shortlisted candidates sit an admission test; follow the chosen ahliya university programme's own requirements.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Only priority fields: medicine, engineering, computing and artificial intelligence, nursing, veterinary medicine, applied arts, arts and design, agriculture, tourism and hotels, and archaeology, at the 32 participating ahliya universities (Cairo, Ain Shams, Alexandria, Mansoura, Assiut, Helwan, Nile, Galala, King Salman, El Alamein, Egypt University of Informatics and other ahliya universities).

nationality.note: Need-based as well as merit-based: open only to Egyptian students who got Thanaweya Amma (or STEM) from a government school in the current year AND benefit from the Takaful and Karama programme or were exempted from school fees by the Ministry of Education that year. Students who hold another funded grant at the same time cannot apply. Grants are spread across all governorates and include people with disabilities.

language.note: No English or other language test is required to apply.

field.note: Available faculties depend on the governorate of the student's school and the student's total score.

timeline.opening_month: Late August (after Thanaweya Amma results and the first phase of public-university coordination)
timeline.typical_deadline: Early September; the window lasts about a week (2026/27: opened 29 Aug, closed Friday 4 Sep 2026 at 7 PM after an extension)
timeline.interview_period: Admission test for provisionally nominated candidates in September (date and place shown on the portal's application-tracking page)
timeline.result_announcement: Names of candidates nominated for the second (admission) stage are published on the portal in September
timeline.course_start: Late September / October (start of the Egyptian academic year)

deadline.label: Online application on the Future Scholars portal
deadline.note: Official ministry statement (1 Sep 2026) extended the 2026/27 call to Friday 4 Sep 2026, 7 PM. Al-Mal News and Banker reported the original window as 29 Aug 2026 (11 AM) to 2 Sep 2026 (5 PM). The 2027 dates are not announced; expect a short window in late August or early September 2027 and watch the portal from mid-August.

application_portal_system: Future Scholars portal (futurescholars.mohesr.gov.eg) – login with national ID + Thanaweya Amma certificate password
strategic_tips: This is the ministry's main scholarship for top students from families on Takaful and Karama or with a school-fee exemption: if that applies to you, prepare scans of the student's and guardian's national IDs and the signed declaration before results day, because the 2026 window lasted about one week. Apply from a computer, and choose faculties you can realistically excel in, since you must pass an admission test and then keep a 3.0 GPA to keep the grant. A faculty in your own governorate is preferred, so families who prefer their daughter to study close to home can rank nearby ahliya universities first.
program_status_note: First cohort admitted in 2025/26 and a second cohort in 2026/27 (ministry and Central Bank meeting of 20 Aug 2026). The older ministry portal for the initiative (egyaid.mohesr.gov.eg, 'مبادرة دعم تكافؤ الفرص في التعليم العالي') now opens this portal. This is a single national programme; it is different from the excellence discounts (منح التفوق) that each private or ahliya university gives to its own top applicants.

name: Dr. Ali Moselhy Educational Grant at National (Ahliya) Universities – Nasser Social Bank (منحة المرحوم الدكتور علي مصيلحي التعليمية)
organization: General Authority of Nasser Social Bank (الهيئة العامة لبنك ناصر الاجتماعي), through the Council of National (Ahliya) Universities, Ministry of Higher Education

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: None stated
coverage_details.additional_allowances: All tuition fees plus free student housing with meals, similar to public university dormitories, at the host ahliya university. 400 grants were announced for 2025/26. Students who already paid first-semester fees and then won the grant were refunded in full (ministry clarification, Jan 2026).

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Egyptian nationals living in Egypt with Thanaweya Amma (first sitting) from government, experimental, STEM or Nile schools, with social need
eligibility.gpa_requirement: A distinguished score within 3 percentage points below the public-university cut-off of the matching faculty (2025/26 rule reported by Masrawy), plus the faculty's admission requirements. Keep an overall grade of 'Very Good' (or the equivalent GPA, about 3.0) throughout the degree.
eligibility.language_requirements: None stated beyond the chosen faculty's admission requirements.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Labour-market priority fields: medicine, nursing, veterinary medicine, health sciences technology, computing/information/AI, agriculture, business administration, tourism, arts and design (and languages in the January 2026 round), at King Salman International University and the Assiut, South Valley, Sohag, New Valley and Luxor ahliya universities.
eligibility.return_obligation: Sign a commitment and repay the grant if any condition is broken (e.g. transferring out of the university).

nationality.note: Social need is required. Priority: students from the neediest governorates, Takaful and Karama families, children in social-care homes, and low-income families (who must prove income with bank statements, family records, lease and six months of utility bills).

timeline.opening_month: Late September (2025/26: 28 September 2025; extra second-semester round in January 2026)
timeline.typical_deadline: Early October (2025/26: 2 October 2025, 10 PM; second-semester round closed 22 January 2026, 10 PM)
timeline.result_announcement: Within days of the deadline (2025/26: 4 October 2025)
timeline.course_start: October (or second semester for the January round)

deadline.note: Official Council of National Universities notice: 400 grants, applications 28 Sep – 2 Oct 2025 (10 PM), results 4 Oct 2025. A second-semester round closed 22 Jan 2026 (Masrawy, 7 Jan 2026). No 2026/27 round was found as of 25 Oct 2026, so the 2027 timing is unknown.

strategic_tips: This grant is a 'last chance' route into an ahliya university in Upper Egypt for strong students from needy families whose score is just below the public-university cut-off for their dream faculty. The window is only a few days, so collect income papers (bank statements, utility bills, lease, Takaful and Karama card) in summer and write your personal statement in advance. Housing and meals are included, which helps families whose daughters must study away from home in a supervised dormitory.
program_status_note: Ran in 2025/26 (September 2025 and January 2026 rounds). No 2026/27 call was found on the Council of National Universities site as of 25 Oct 2026 (the 2025 notice is marked expired). Keep it on the watch-list for the 2027 cycle.

name: Nile University Undergraduate Scholarships (منح جامعة النيل الأهلية)
organization: Nile University (NU), Sheikh Zayed, Giza

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: None for NU merit scholarships; partner-funded scholarships (e.g. Sawiris Foundation) add stipends
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Full merit scholarship (100% for the whole programme, keep CGPA 3.0): 50 students from the top 500 Thanaweya Amma graduates nationally and 20 students from the top STEM-school graduates. MoU-sponsored full scholarships from partners: Sawiris Distinction Scholarship (tuition, stipend, books, laptop, housing for students from other governorates; all schools except Biotechnology) and the Egyptian Refining Company 'Mostaqbali' scholarship (students from El Matariya, El Khosos and East Shoubra El Kheima, School of Engineering). Partial: first-year merit scholarship of 50%, 40% or 20% by Thanaweya Amma score (then applied by CGPA), 10% early admission, 10% school MoU, 10% events, 10% siblings, 10% government employees' children, sports scholarships; up to 3 partial awards combined, maximum 60%. Need-based tuition aid for continuing students.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Full merit scholarships: Egyptian Thanaweya Amma graduates (Arts, Science and Math sections) and STEM-school graduates; partial scholarships apply to all certificates
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Full scholarship: be among the top 500 nationally ranked Thanaweya Amma students (proof of national ranking) or among the top STEM-school graduates, with a strong record of extracurricular activities, research, innovation, entrepreneurship or volunteering; keep CGPA 3.0. Partial merit 50/40/20% depends on the Thanaweya Amma score (thresholds not published on the page). Selection weighs the high-school score, financial need, extracurricular awards and an interview.
eligibility.language_requirements: Meet NU admission requirements including English: applicants book the NU English placement test during the online application.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Business, Engineering and Applied Sciences, Information Technology and Computer Science, Biotechnology (Sawiris-funded places exclude Biotechnology).
eligibility.return_obligation: Sawiris-funded places: work in Egypt for 3 years after graduation.

nationality.note: Full merit and partner scholarships are for Egyptian Thanaweya Amma / STEM graduates; preference for incoming high-school graduates over transfer students.

language.note: NU English placement test booked and paid for in the online application; no IELTS minimum is published for undergraduates.

timeline.opening_month: Summer, around the Thanaweya Amma results (exact opening date not published)
timeline.typical_deadline: Early August (2026/27 scholarship form closed 8 August 2026)
timeline.interview_period: Shortlisted candidates may be invited to an interview

deadline.label: Scholarship application form (after the NU admission application gives you an NU ID)
deadline.note: The NU page now says 'Application closed for 2026'; Al-Watan (1 Aug 2026) and search snippets of the NU page reported the 2026/27 deadline as 8 Aug 2026. The Sawiris Distinction Scholarship has its own deadline (14 Aug 2026 for 2026/27). Expect a similar early-August deadline for Fall 2027.

strategic_tips: Apply for admission first to get your NU ID, then submit the scholarship form before the early-August deadline; incomplete or late forms are not considered. Only 50 full places go to the top 500 Thanaweya Amma students and 20 to STEM graduates, so collect certificates for olympiads, research, volunteering and competitions to stand out at the interview. Public-school students scoring 90%+ should also apply for the Sawiris Distinction Scholarship at NU, which adds a stipend, laptop and housing.
program_status_note: Postgraduate: NU offers only one named full scholarship a year (the 'Mohamed Samy' scholarship for the Master of Information Technology and Computer Science, deadline 20 Aug 2025 for Fall 2025); it is not modelled here.

name: Sawiris Distinction Scholarship for Public High School Graduates (منحة ساويرس للتميز)
organization: Sawiris Foundation for Social Development (مؤسسة ساويرس للتنمية الاجتماعية), managed for cohort 6 by Aspire for Strategic Solutions

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Stipend included (amount not published)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Tuition fees; stipend, books, educational materials and a laptop; accommodation for students studying outside their home governorate; accessibility equipment as needed; English skills development programmes. Up to 50 scholarships per cohort, for the full length of study.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Egyptian nationals residing in Egypt (dual nationals are not given preference) who have not lived abroad for more than three years
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Graduate of an Egyptian public Thanaweya Amma school in the current year with a score of at least 90% (about 3.6 on a 4.0 scale). Priority to financial need, academic excellence, extracurricular activities and Takaful and Karama beneficiaries.
eligibility.language_requirements: Only for English-taught programmes: the minimum English level required by the university.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Engineering, science, information technology, economics and political science, commerce, mass communication, law, agriculture and nursing, at the partner universities: Ain Shams, Alexandria, Assiut, E-JUST, Zewail City, Nile University (not Biotechnology), Egypt University of Informatics, Galala, the British University in Egypt (BUE) and Agora University.
eligibility.return_obligation: Must commit to work in Egypt for 3 years after graduation and complete military service where applicable.

nationality.note: Public-school Thanaweya Amma graduates only. Open to all governorates, with priority for Fayoum, Minya, Assiut, Sohag and Qena.

language.note: English proof only if the chosen programme is taught in English (e.g. Zewail City, Nile University, BUE, E-JUST).

timeline.opening_month: Summer, after Thanaweya Amma results (exact opening date not published)
timeline.typical_deadline: Mid-August (2026/27 cohort 6: 14 August 2026, 5 PM)

deadline.label: Online Sawiris Distinction Scholarship application (5 PM)
deadline.note: Official page: 'deadline is 14 August 2026 – 5 PM' for cohort 6 (2026/2027). The cohort 7 (2027/28) call is not yet published; expect a similar mid-August deadline after Thanaweya Amma results.

strategic_tips: Apply to the partner university's programme first, then fill the Sawiris form before the mid-August deadline with your placement number ready; a nomination does not guarantee university admission. Students from Fayoum, Minya, Assiut, Sohag and Qena and Takaful and Karama families get priority, and the award pays housing if you study outside your governorate, so families can still choose a partner university close to home (Assiut, Alexandria, Ain Shams). Remember the 3-year work-in-Egypt commitment after graduation.
program_status_note: Cohort 6 ran for 2026/27. The foundation also runs other programmes not modelled here: the Yousriya Loza-Sawiris Scholarship (postgraduate), executive-education and TVET scholarships, and the StARTing Point arts residency.

name: Zewail City Postgraduate Scholarships (منح الدراسات العليا بمدينة زويل – ماجستير ودكتوراه)
organization: University of Science and Technology (UST), Zewail City of Science, Technology and Innovation – Postgraduate Scholarship Evaluation Committee

coverage_details.additional_allowances: Competitive tuition scholarships for admitted MSc and PhD students; the share of tuition covered is not published. name: Zewail City Undergraduate Scholarships (منح مدينة زويل – البكالوريوس)
organization: University of Science and Technology (UST), Zewail City of Science, Technology and Innovation

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: None for merit discounts; partner-funded full scholarships may add housing or other costs depending on the funder
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Three routes. (1) Merit scholarship, first year (2026/27 tables): Engineering – Science section 90%+ or Math section 85%+ = 50% off, Science 80–90% or Math 75–85% = 25% off; Science and Computational Science & AI schools – 90%+ = 50%, 80–90% = 25%; Business – 85%+ = 50%, 75–85% = 25% (Thanaweya Amma, Azharia and STEM). From year 2 the discount follows the cumulative GPA: 4.00 = 100%, 3.80 = 50%, 3.50 = 25%, below 3.50 = 0%. Average annual fees before discount 2026/27: Engineering 173,880 EGP, Science 141,120 EGP, CSAI 137,984 EGP, Business 112,000 EGP. (2) Up to two of the top 10 Thanaweya Amma students of each governorate get a full scholarship for four years while keeping a CGPA of 3.00. (3) Funded full scholarships (Sawiris Foundation, Egyptian Refining Company, Youssef Mansour and Family – 30 places in Computational Science & AI, Faisal Bank) cover tuition in full; housing depends on the funder. Other discounts: 25% first year for Business or Science applicants, 10% for siblings, children of government employees and top-3 national sports ranks. Only one discount per student; discounts cannot be combined.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Egyptian students with Thanaweya Amma, Azharia, STEM or equivalent certificates (American Diploma, IGCSE, IB, French, Canadian, German, Nile schools have their own tables); non-Egyptians pay in USD with separate rules
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Merit discount by school-leaving score: 50% for Thanaweya Amma Science 90%+ / Math 85%+ (Engineering), 25% for Science 80–90% / Math 75–85%. Full scholarships go to up to two of the top 10 students per governorate, or through funded scholarships (academic excellence, financial need where the funder requires it, interview). Admission itself needs the yearly minimum score plus passing the Zewail admission test. Converted roughly: 75% ≈ 3.0, 85–90% ≈ 3.5–3.6 on a 4.0 scale.
eligibility.language_requirements: Evidence of English proficiency (IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT or PTE Academic) or the Zewail City English Placement Test; weaker students are placed in English courses.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Schools of Engineering; Science (incl. biomedical sciences, physics, materials, nanoscience); Computational Science & Artificial Intelligence; Business.
eligibility.return_obligation: Funded scholarships: a scholarship agreement co-signed by the guardian as financial guarantor; withdrawal without approval may have to be repaid. The Sawiris-funded route requires 3 years of work in Egypt after graduation.

nationality.note: Merit tables and funded scholarships on the official pages are for Egyptian applicants; international students have a separate USD fee table.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: This record covers applicants whose country of origin is Egypt (DAAD Regional Office Cairo). The programme exists for many countries with their own deadlines.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Above-average qualifications. Option a) sandwich model: Master's or Diplom (exceptionally Bachelor's) by the funding start. Option b) cotutelle: admitted to a doctoral programme by the funding start.
eligibility.language_requirements: Proof of English (TOEFL iBT 79, IELTS 6.5, onSET B2 or PTE 59) if the project is in English; German if the working language is German
eligibility.age_limit: No age limit, but the most recent degree should as a rule be no more than 6 years old at the deadline; a doctorate already started should have begun no more than 3 years before applying
eligibility.field_restrictions: All fields (separate rules for human medicine, veterinary medicine and dentistry). The doctorate is awarded by the home university (option a, sandwich model) or jointly with the German university (option b, cotutelle).

nationality.note: The deadline in this record is DAAD's deadline for applicants from Egypt. Other nationalities can apply with their own country deadlines. Not eligible if resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the deadline.

language.note: English proof only if the project is in English; German-language projects need German.

field.note: Human medicine, veterinary medicine and dentistry follow special rules.

timeline.typical_deadline: 31 August for applicants from Egypt
timeline.course_start: Funding from October of the following year

deadline.label: DAAD portal deadline for applicants from Egypt (24:00 CET/CEST)
deadline.note: Official DAAD database (country of origin Egypt): applications 1 June - 31 Aug 2026, selection Feb 2027, funding starts Oct 2027. Already passed for 2027; DAAD says deadlines usually stay in the same period, so expect about 31 Aug 2027.

documents.label: Online application in the DAAD portal
Full curriculum vitae in tabular form (max. 3 pages)
List of published publications (max. 10 pages), if applicable
Letter of motivation (1-2 pages)
Research proposal discussed with the German academic adviser (max. 10 pages)
Schedule for the whole funding period, showing how time is split between Germany and the home university

Option a) confirmation signed by both supervisors guaranteeing a workplace in Germany; option b) cotutelle contract between the two universities (or the German adviser's confirmation until it is ready)
Declaration from the German supervisor on safety-relevant and ethical aspects of the project
Proof of admission to / enrolment in doctoral studies at the home university, with start date (if applicable)
All university degree certificates with final grades
Transcripts of records for undergraduate and postgraduate studies
One recent letter of recommendation from a university teacher (DAAD form)
Valid identification document (passport needed for the visa)
English proof if the project is in English
documents.notes: Required only for English-language projects.

application_portal_system: DAAD portal (online application, 1 June - 31 August for Egypt)
strategic_tips: Good fit if you are (or will be) a PhD student or assistant lecturer at an Egyptian university and want German supervision without leaving your post: you stay enrolled at home and spend 7-24 funded months in Germany. Agree the project and the split between Egypt and Germany with both supervisors before June. A formal cotutelle contract takes months to sign, so start it early or apply under the simpler sandwich option.

name: Egyptian Government Scholarships for International Students (EGYAID / Study in Egypt) - منح الحكومة المصرية للطلاب الوافدين
organization: Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research of Egypt (Study in Egypt / Central Administration for International Students), announced through partner-country ministries and Egyptian embassies

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: None stated (2025/26 call: living expenses are the student's responsibility)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Tuition and registration fees only (2025/26 EGYAID call). Full tuition becomes effective after passing the preparatory year; if the student fails it, only 50% of tuition is covered. Some bilateral country quotas are announced as 'fully funded'; check your own country's announcement.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Non-Egyptian nationals. Places are usually allocated per country and announced by the partner country's ministry or the Egyptian embassy (2026/27 notices seen from Algeria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Liberia).
eligibility.gpa_requirement: At least a 'Good' ('Bien') grade in the previous degree and meeting the Egyptian university's admission requirements
eligibility.language_requirements: No test fixed in the call. Most public-university programmes are taught in Arabic; English-taught programmes follow each university's rules.
eligibility.age_limit: Must not exceed 22 (undergraduate), 30 (Master's) or 35 (PhD) (2025/26 call)
eligibility.field_restrictions: Scientific, technical and literary fields at Egyptian universities, depending on the country quota and the call

nationality.note: For foreign nationals coming to Egypt. Applicants must not have had a similar Egyptian government scholarship before. Seats and levels depend on your country's quota, so check the announcement from your ministry or the Egyptian embassy. Source is the official 2025/26 EGYAID call text as relayed by a partner-country public university (the Study in Egypt portal itself does not publish the call text).

language.note: Arabic is needed for Arabic-taught programmes; English programmes follow university rules. A separate EGYAID Arabic Language Center scholarship exists for ages 15-27 (placement test).

field.note: Depends on the country quota and the programmes offered in the call.

timeline.opening_month: Summer (about June to August; relayed by partner-country ministries)
timeline.typical_deadline: Mid-September on the Study in Egypt platform; some countries set an earlier national deadline (e.g. 31 August)

deadline.label: Study in Egypt (EGYAID) online registration

extra.label: Earlier national deadline in some partner countries (e.g. Bosnia and Herzegovina, 31 Aug 2026)

deadline.note: Official partner notices: 2025/26 call deadline 15 Sep 2025 (Algeria, Univ. Mostaganem relay); 2026/27 platform registration deadline 15 Sep 2026 (Algeria, Univ. Oum El Bouaghi relay, PhD offer); Bosnia and Herzegovina's ministry gave 31 Aug 2026 (fmks.gov.ba). Both have passed. The 2027/28 call is not yet published; expect a similar mid-August to mid-September window.

documents.label: Online application on the Study in Egypt (EGYAID) platform, plus your country's national form if it has one
Motivation letter
Certified copies of degrees obtained
Certified secondary-school certificate
Certified transcripts
Certificate of good conduct
Recent medical certificate
Copy of valid passport
Two letters of recommendation
Letter of acceptance or pre-admission from an Egyptian university (if available)

application_portal_system: Study in Egypt admission platform (admission.study-in-egypt.gov.eg), often plus a national nomination by your own ministry
strategic_tips: Ask your Ministry of Higher Education or the Egyptian embassy from June which levels and how many seats your country has, because each country gets its own quota and sometimes an earlier deadline. Budget for living costs, housing, travel and insurance: the standard EGYAID award only pays tuition and registration fees. Check the language of your programme; most public-university degrees are taught in Arabic.

name: Rifaa Al-Tahtawi Master's Scholarship (French Embassy in Egypt) - منحة رفاعة الطهطاوي للماجستير في فرنسا
organization: Embassy of France in Egypt / Institut français d'Égypte (French Government scholarship)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: €860/month for up to 10 months (2023-24 call; check the current call)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Exemption from tuition fees at public higher education institutions (up to €5,000); student social security; help to get a room in a student residence (rent at the student's expense). Travel is not covered.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Egyptian nationals (French-Egyptian dual nationals are not eligible)
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Outstanding academic performance; graduated from an Egyptian or French higher education institution, or in the final year of at least 4 years of undergraduate study (Bac+4)
eligibility.language_requirements: B2 in English and/or French (DELF, DALF, TCF, TEF, IELTS, TOEFL, TOEIC), OR a secondary diploma taught in English/French (French Bac, IGCSE, IB, SAT, AP...), OR a university letter stating your studies were taught in English or French
eligibility.field_restrictions: Any field, but only for a second-year Master's (M2) with courses in France; work-study (alternance) and distance programmes are not eligible; one Tahtawi scholarship per person

nationality.note: Egyptian nationality; French-Egyptian dual nationals are excluded. Past Tahtawi scholars cannot apply again. Priority to students going abroad for the first time.

language.note: B2 English or French certificate, or an English/French-taught secondary diploma, or a university letter (English/French medium).

field.note: Master 2 programmes in France only.

timeline.typical_deadline: Mid-February to end of March

deadline.label: Tahtawi scholarship application (23:30 Cairo time in 2026)
deadline.note: 2026-27 (14th call): deadline 15 Feb 2026, 23:30 Cairo time (French Embassy announcement relayed by Mansoura University). 2023-24 call: 15 Jan - 15 Mar 2023 (official call PDF). The 2027-28 call is not yet published; the 15 Feb date is an estimate from the latest call.

documents.label: Application to one or more Master 2 programmes in France (via Études en France or directly) and proof of it (Études en France file number, receipt or acceptance)
Online information form for the Tahtawi programme
Copy of passport (identity page)
CV, maximum 1 page, in English or French
Cover letter describing the study project (max. 1 page, Times New Roman 12, same language as the CV)
Transcript of the high-school diploma (Thanaweya Amma, French Bac, other)
Transcripts of all university years, with French or English translation if in Arabic
Last diploma obtained, with French or English translation if in Arabic
B2 language certificate in English or French (or accepted alternatives)

application_portal_system: Études en France (programme applications) + Tahtawi form, with the file emailed to the Institut français d'Égypte (bourses@ifegypte.com in the 2023 call)
strategic_tips: Apply to your M2 programmes through Études en France from November, because you need a file number or proof of application before the Tahtawi deadline. The selection weighs grades first, then how your M2 fits your previous studies and career plan, then extracurriculars, so keep the cover letter to one sharp page. Budget for flights and rent, which the scholarship does not pay.
program_status_note: The 2027-28 call has not been published yet (as of 25 Oct 2026). Benefits and documents are from the latest official call PDF (2023-24) and may change.

name: GREAT Scholarships - Egypt (£10,000-£15,000 towards a UK Master's)
organization: British Council and the UK Government's GREAT Britain Campaign, jointly with UK universities

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: None (tuition award only)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: £10,000 towards tuition fees for a one-year taught master's (£15,000 at Imperial College London in 2026-27), paid by the university after registration. Welcome and networking events for GREAT scholars.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Passport holders and permanent residents of Egypt (Egypt track; GREAT also runs separate tracks for 17 other countries)
eligibility.gpa_requirement: An undergraduate degree, motivation and interest in the subject; meet the university's entry requirements (no fixed GPA)
eligibility.language_requirements: Meet the English language requirement of the UK university
eligibility.field_restrictions: One-year taught master's courses chosen by each university. Egypt 2026-27: Imperial College London (all full-time taught master's), Keele, Nottingham Trent, Teesside, Sheffield Hallam, Essex, Southampton, University of the West of England.

nationality.note: Egypt track: must be a passport holder AND permanent resident of Egypt. GREAT runs separate country tracks (18 countries in 2026-27) with different universities.

language.note: Set by each university (IELTS or equivalent).

field.note: Eligible courses differ by university; check each university's GREAT page.

timeline.opening_month: Autumn/winter before the intake (university pages update for each cycle)
timeline.typical_deadline: January to May of the intake year (set by each university)
timeline.result_announcement: Each university informs its scholars, usually in late spring or summer

deadline.label: Earliest university GREAT deadline for Egypt (2026-27: Teesside 24 Apr; others 30 Apr - 31 May)

extra.label: Imperial: submit the master's application by about 7 January to be considered
Latest university GREAT deadline (2026-27: Sheffield Hallam 31 May)

deadline.note: 2026-27 Egypt deadlines from the official Study UK university pages: Imperial 7 Jan 2026 (course application, decision by 13 Mar), Teesside 24 Apr, Southampton 30 Apr, UWE Bristol 1 May, Keele 15 May, Nottingham Trent 27 May, Essex 30 May, Sheffield Hallam 31 May 2026. The 2027-28 university list and deadlines are NOT yet published (as of 25 Oct 2026); the dates above are estimates from the 2026 pattern.

documents.label: Application to an eligible one-year taught master's at the participating university
GREAT Scholarship application on the university's scholarship page (format varies by university)
Egyptian passport (passport holder and permanent resident of Egypt)
Undergraduate degree certificate
Academic transcripts
Proof of English meeting the university's requirement
documents.notes: Whether an English-medium letter is accepted depends on the university.

documents.label: Offer for the master's course (many universities only consider offer holders)

application_portal_system: Each participating university's own scholarship application (links from the Study UK Egypt page)
strategic_tips: GREAT covers only part of the tuition, so budget for the rest of the fees and UK living costs, or combine it with other funding. Apply to the course early: most universities only consider applicants who already hold an offer, and Imperial needs the course application in early January. Check the Study UK Egypt page in winter 2026-27 for the new list of universities, then apply to several of them.
program_status_note: 2027-28 participating universities for Egypt are not yet announced (as of 25 Oct 2026); the list changes every year.

name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the American University in Cairo (Master's)
organization: Mastercard Foundation and The American University in Cairo (AUC)

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Stipend during the fall and spring semesters (amount not published)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Tuition for 9 credits per semester; laptop; student services and activities fees; medical service and health insurance fees; dorm room for scholars living outside Cairo; AUC bus subscription or travel allowance; remedial or intensive English if needed; round-trip airfare for scholars not residing in Egypt; possible funding for research, publication fees and conferences; IT/software support for students with disabilities; leadership workshops.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Citizens of at least one African country (Egyptians included) who currently reside in an African country
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Bachelor's degree with a minimum overall GPA of 3.2 on a 4.0 scale or equivalent; keep 3.2 during studies
eligibility.language_requirements: AUC graduate full admission: TOEFL iBT 79 (writing 21) or IELTS Academic 6.5 (writing 7); remedial English may be covered
eligibility.age_limit: 35 or younger at the time of application
eligibility.field_restrictions: Any AUC graduate field; new degree-seeking students only (transfers not eligible)

nationality.note: Citizenship of at least one African country AND current residence in an African country. Financial need must be shown. Separate from the Mastercard Foundation partners abroad (see mastercard-foundation).

language.note: AUC admission cut-offs: IELTS 6.5 (writing 7) or TOEFL iBT 79 (writing 21); the program may fund remedial English.

field.note: Any AUC graduate programme (new degree-seeking students only).

timeline.opening_month: December (Fall cycle 1), April (Fall cycle 2), October (Spring cycle)
timeline.typical_deadline: Fall intake: 17 January (cycle 1) or 6 May (cycle 2); Spring intake: 2 November
timeline.course_start: September (Fall) or February (Spring); program starts Spring 2027

deadline.label: AUC fellowship application, Fall 2027 cycle 1 (submit the graduate admission application at least 2 weeks earlier)

extra.label: Submit the AUC graduate admission application (at least 2 weeks before the fellowship deadline)
Fall cycle 2 fellowship deadline (if places remain)

deadline.note: The Mastercard Foundation page sends applicants to AUC's fellowship calendar (updated 23 Aug 2026): Fall 2027 cycle 1 opens 22 Dec, deadline 17 Jan 2027; cycle 2 opens 6 Apr, deadline 6 May 2027. The first intake is Spring 2027 (cycle 7 Oct - 2 Nov 2026, now passed).

documents.label: AUC graduate online application (ApplyWeb) with application fee
Official Mastercard Foundation Scholars online application (AUC Banner)
Statement of purpose (about 500 words for each programme selected)
Updated resume (CV) with work experience and education
At least two online letters of recommendation
Official final bachelor's transcript with stamps and signatures (English or officially translated)
Proof of bachelor's degree completion
TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic or Cambridge CAE/CPE results
Passport information pages (international applicants) or national ID (Egyptians)
Proof of financial need (additional paperwork may be requested)

application_portal_system: AUC ApplyWeb (admission) + AUC Banner (Mastercard Foundation Scholars application)
strategic_tips: This is one of the few full master's scholarships that Egyptians can use at home, as well as Africans coming to Cairo. Show financial need clearly and a give-back plan for your community, since the program looks for leadership and impact. Apply for AUC admission by early January, then submit the scholarship form before 17 January 2027 for Fall 2027.

name: Tomorrow's Leaders Undergraduate Scholarship (U.S. State Department MEPI) at AUB / LAU, Lebanon - منحة قادة الغد
organization: U.S. Department of State Middle East Partnership Initiative (MEPI), administered by FHI 360

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Monthly living stipend when participating in TL activities (amount not published)
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Tuition and enrolment fees for up to four academic years; university health insurance; entrance visa and residency permit fees; student housing; textbook allowance; laptop; two round-trip tickets home per year; career workshops, internships and faculty mentorship; possible semester in the United States; TOEFL/SAT costs for shortlisted finalists.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Citizens of Algeria, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Syria, Tunisia, the West Bank (or Palestinian students legally resident in a third country) and Yemen; U.S. citizens and U.S. permanent residents are not eligible
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Strong academic credentials; generally 80% or better across your academic history (partner-university standards); keep a 3.0 GPA during studies
eligibility.language_requirements: Free online ASU English assessment with the application; shortlisted finalists need TOEFL iBT 80 (4.0 on the new scale) or IELTS by 8 March 2027 (cost covered). Duolingo accepted by LAU only.
eligibility.age_limit: Current high-school seniors or students who graduated from high school in 2026 (2025 graduates only from Iraq, Libya, Syria, the West Bank/Palestinians abroad and Yemen)
eligibility.field_restrictions: Undergraduate fields offered at the American University of Beirut and the Lebanese American University (medicine is not eligible)

nationality.note: Palestine = West Bank, or Palestinian students legally resident in a third country; students currently residing in Gaza cannot apply this cycle. Citizens of these countries living elsewhere may apply (except U.S. permanent residents). Egyptian applicants must be high-school seniors or 2026 graduates.

language.note: Only the free ASU online test is needed to apply; TOEFL iBT 80 / IELTS for finalists by 8 Mar 2027.

field.note: Any AUB/LAU undergraduate major except medicine.

timeline.typical_deadline: Mid-November (18 November 2026 for 2027-28)
timeline.interview_period: January (online interviews with FHI 360, U.S. Embassy staff and alumni)

deadline.label: Tomorrow's Leaders online application

extra.label: Shortlisted: TOEFL or IELTS results due
Shortlisted: SAT scores due (select majors and American-style schools)

deadline.note: Official FAQ and timeline for the 2027-28 cohort: applications 1 Oct - 18 Nov 2026 (OPEN as of 25 Oct 2026); initial review Dec 2026; interviews Jan 2027; TOEFL/IELTS by 8 Mar 2027 and SAT by 26 Mar 2027 for finalists; conditional offers May-Jul 2027; pre-departure orientation and travel Aug 2027.

documents.label: Tomorrow's Leaders online application (all applicable sections)
Personal statement (part of the online application)
Official school transcripts for grades 10 and 11 (and 12 when available), with English translation
High-school graduation certificate/diploma (2026 graduates now; current seniors when available)
Documentation of extracurricular and/or volunteer activities
Free online ASU English assessment (taken once, about 30 minutes, same email as the application)
Recommendation from an academic reference (teacher or school administrator)
Second recommendation (teacher, coach, volunteer supervisor; not friends or family)
National ID card (accepted for the online application)
TOEFL iBT (80 / 4.0) or IELTS results for shortlisted finalists, by 8 March 2027 (program pays)
SAT I or SAT II scores (select majors and American-style school students), by 26 March 2027
Passport (shortlisted applicants are asked to get one)

application_portal_system: Tomorrow's Leaders online application (FHI 360); no separate AUB/LAU application needed
strategic_tips: Open now for Egyptian high-school seniors and 2026 graduates, closing 18 November 2026: ask two recommenders this week (at least one teacher) and take the ASU English test once, in a quiet place. Show leadership with documented activities, because selection weighs leadership potential as much as grades. You must be willing to study at either AUB or LAU in Beirut.

name: USAID Scholarships in Egypt (Higher Education Initiative, USAID Scholars, Egyptian Pioneers) - منح الوكالة الأمريكية للتنمية الدولية (متوقفة)
organization: U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) Egypt, implemented with The American University in Cairo (AUC), Amideast and Egypt's Ministry of Higher Education

coverage_details.monthly_stipend: Historical only: monthly stipend (amount varied by track). No new awards.
coverage_details.additional_allowances: Historical only: undergraduate tracks at Egyptian universities covered tuition, a monthly stipend and university housing; graduate tracks (Master's in the U.S. or Egypt) also covered U.S. study costs. Health insurance, airfare and visa coverage differed by track and are not recorded here because the program has ended.

eligibility.eligible_nationalities: Egyptian citizens only (historically: public, experimental and STEM school graduates from underserved governorates for undergraduate tracks; mid-career government professionals for Master's/postdoctoral tracks)
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Historically high Thanaweya Amma scores (undergraduate) or a strong academic record (graduate). No current call.
eligibility.language_requirements: Historically English proficiency for AUC or U.S. study. No current call.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Historically STEM, business and development-related fields chosen with the Egyptian government. No current call.
eligibility.return_obligation: Historically scholars were expected to serve Egypt after graduation (U.S. J-1 rules applied to U.S. study).

nationality.note: The program is DISCONTINUED. The Egyptian-only rule is kept so the record explains the program to Egyptians who still ask about it.

language.note: No current call, so no language rule applies.

field.note: No current call.

timeline.opening_month: No longer opens (last calls before the January 2025 aid freeze)
timeline.typical_deadline: None: the program has ended. USAID stopped implementing foreign assistance on 1 July 2025.

documents.label: USAID scholarship application (no longer accepted)
documents.notes: Kept for reference only. There is no open call.

documents.label: Egyptian national ID
documents.notes: Kept for reference only.

documents.label: Thanaweya Amma / STEM school certificate (undergraduate tracks)
documents.notes: Kept for reference only.

documents.label: University transcripts (graduate tracks)
documents.notes: Kept for reference only.

application_portal_system: None (closed). Formerly AUC and Ministry of Higher Education online applications.
strategic_tips: This program no longer takes applications, so do not plan around it. Similar U.S.-linked options for Egyptians that are still running: Tomorrow's Leaders (U.S. State Department undergraduate scholarship at AUB/LAU, deadline 18 Nov 2026), Fulbright Egypt (graduate study in the U.S.), the Onsi Sawiris scholarships run by Amideast Egypt, and the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at AUC. If you were already a USAID scholar, ask your university's scholarship office: the Ministry of Higher Education said in early 2025 that universities would keep covering existing scholars.
program_status_note: Discontinued: U.S. foreign aid was frozen in January 2025 and the State Department announced that USAID would 'officially cease to implement foreign assistance' on 1 July 2025. usaid.gov (including usaid.gov/egypt) now shows only the February 2025 staff administrative-leave notice, and AUC's public USAID Scholars pages are offline (they redirect to a login page). No new USAID scholarship calls (Higher Education Initiative public-university and graduate scholarships, LEAD, USAID Scholars Activity at AUC, USAID Egyptian Pioneers) are expected. Egyptian universities and the Ministry of Higher Education said they would cover students who were already on these awards (press reports, Jan-Apr 2025).
